pages.title: Browser Support
pages.markdown:
# Browser Support

## Supported Browsers

We actively test the editor in all major web browsers. Report any issue in the browsers below as a bug on [our GitHub repository](https://www.github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor/).

| Browser or system | Supported versions |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome | Current and previous |
| Safari | Current and previous |
| Microsoft Edge | Current and previous |
| Firefox | Current and previous |
| Opera | Current and previous |
| Internet Explorer | 11 |
| iOS | 10 and later |
| Android | 6 and later |

Current and previous means the current stable version of the browser and the version before it.

## Unsupported Browsers

- **Pre-release versions.** We don't support beta or dev releases of a browser. If you find a bug in one, report it to the browser vendor.
- **Older versions.** The editor may run in older browser versions without major issues, but we don't test it in them and usually don't fix bugs that appear there.

## How We Test

We test the editor constantly in every supported browser with unit tests. Browsers behave in slightly different ways, so small differences from one browser to another can remain.

Testing is essential to fully support a browser. [BrowserStack](https://www.browserstack.com/) offers virtual machines for testing many browser versions on different platforms.

## Editor Versions

Only the latest version of the editor is tested and updated with bug fixes and new features. If you find a bug in an older version, upgrade to [the latest release](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/changelog/) first to see whether it is already fixed.

## Fonts not Showing in Firefox

If you are working locally and testing examples using `file:///` in the browser instead of running files from a web server, the icons might not show up properly in Firefox. This is because Firefox has a strict “file URI origin” policy that blocks web fonts stored in a folder above the page’s own folder (for example, `../fonts/`). Fonts stored in the same folder as the HTML page, or in one of its subfolders, are not affected and will load normally.

# Changelog Every release of the editor since 4.0.0, newest first, with what it added and what it fixed. Each date is the day the release reached npm. To install a release, name its version. ```shell npm install froala-editor@5.5.0 ``` ## 5.5.0 (Sep 30, 2026) ### New and Improved - Headless mode for the editor, with an initial, limited set of features - AI image generation and insertion - Track changes support for edit actions within element-specific popups (images, videos, links) - The selection stays highlighted while focus moves to other input fields inside the editor - Support for collaborative suggestion mode (track changes) when resizing images and videos ### Fixed - The collaborative panel expanded unexpectedly for users - The floating Add comment button was not displayed on mobile devices when text was selected - Wrong cursor position when selecting text with the collaboration plugin enabled - AI Chat web search and reasoning toggles remain active for models that declare `webSearch: false` or `reasoning: false` - Issue with undo and redo after a browser spell check correction - Page break and drag handle issues when the editor is inside a table or `box-sizing: border-box` is applied - The first IME-composed character is lost when typing into an empty block with `fontSizeDefaultSelection` set (Windows) - Issue with the clear formatting feature - In collaboration, Ctrl+X does not fill the clipboard for tracked changes - In the collaboration plugin, inserted tables are not wrapped in suggestion tags, so tracked changes are lost after reinitialization - Bold and italic formatting in list items is stored as `
  • ` styles instead of inline `` and `` elements - The comments dropdown displays an incorrect Show Open label [Download 5.5.0 on GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor/releases/tag/v5.5.0) ## 5.4.0 (Aug 19, 2026) ### New and Improved - AI Chat Assistant for Froala Editor - Code Snippet Tracking - Drag and Drop Tracking - Markdown editing that keeps Markdown as the source format - Improvements to AI shortcuts and AI content insertion - Speech to text for AI Assist - AI Improve Writing, with changes to accept or reject - AI autofill of content while typing ### Fixed - Issue with the cursor icon when performing undo/redo actions - Issue with the user name tooltip on the cursor - Nested table is removed when pasting copied list item content into a table cell - Cancel and Reply buttons are missing in the comment pop-up - Issue with changing a word using the browser spell check - Issue with removing text formatting in the image caption - Bottom borders are missing after rendering in the Froala Editor - Missing table alignment styles in `froala_style.css` cause incorrect front-end rendering - Linked text appears duplicated after link insertion in the Froala Angular editor inside a PWA - Image caption HTML export includes `contenteditable="true"`, so captions stay editable outside the editor - Ordered list numbering font family changes to Aptos when pasting content from Microsoft Word - Images are not preserved when pasting content from Microsoft Word using a custom Base64 image upload handler - Paste not working when the text to paste is longer than `charCounterMax` - `applyStyle` does not keep the outer-wrap behavior of version 2 for `contentEditable="false"` elements - Table cell alignment applies to the entire `` instead of individual lines when there is no text selection [Download 5.4.0 on GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor/releases/tag/v5.4.0) ## 5.3.1 (Jul 15, 2026) ### New and Improved - Enhanced synchronization and editing experience in Collaborative Editing [Download 5.3.1 on GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor/releases/tag/v5.3.1) ## 5.3.0 (Jul 8, 2026) ### New and Improved - An editable custom font size input in the font size dropdown - A configurable Mammoth instance in the Import from Word plugin, for module-based builds such as Vite - Svelte plugin - Collaborative editing plugin ### Fixed - Microsoft Word ordered list numbering not preserved when pasting content into Froala Editor - List item indent increasing when backspaced - Table style dropdown issue with custom options - Popup position offset when using `toolbarSticky: true` with `scrollableContainer` in a flex layout - Formatting toolbar state becomes inconsistent after deleting content with `keepFormatOnDelete` enabled - Leading spaces added when pasting unformatted text from Microsoft Word - Ordered list numbering does not inherit applied font size - Indent option disabled for list items - Upload Image button remains hidden after window resize, and toolbar does not restore correctly - Clipboard content persisted in `localStorage`, raising potential compliance concerns - Image caption detached from the image when applying styling (background color, bold, italic and others) - Table UI issues, dropdown text not wrapping and the table properties panel opening outside the document view - Underline formatting applied to entire content instead of selected text - Word counter allows exceeding max limit when adding spaces or line breaks before punctuation - Ctrl+Backspace issue in Firefox, and a console error when applying styling - UI issue with pop-ups in dark theme - Issue with the List and Bold features - Browser spellcheck correction removes adjacent text when URL plugin is enabled [Download 5.3.0 on GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor/releases/tag/v5.3.0) ## 5.2.0 (May 13, 2026) ### New and Improved - Filerobot Image Editor integration ### Fixed - Page scrolls to the bottom when dragging the Find and Replace popup - Issues with `toolbarBottom: true` and the table edit popup in `scrollableContainer` - Vulnerability in serialize-javascript, upgraded to 7.0.3 - Inconsistent strikethrough behavior - Formatting not kept for list items when pasting from a Word document - Images from MS Word lose their height and width attributes when `iframeStyleFiles` is configured - Toolbar buttons responsive state changes when refreshing the editor frame - Styled image formatting lost on copy and paste (Firefox and Chrome) - Inline styles generated by the editor are blocked in strict CSP environments without unsafe-inline (partly fixed) - RTL direction not kept when pasting or importing Arabic content from Word - Valid image removed after pasting an invalid file following consecutive image uploads - Tick icon not displayed in color picker without Font Awesome - Editor fails to handle inline styles containing newline characters (`\n`) - Pasting text and images from web pages does not update the editor state in 5.0.1 - The AI shortcut feature stays disabled after generating content - Numbered list resets on Tab and incorrect behavior when removing list numbering with Backspace - Underline formatting from DOCX is not kept when using the Import from DOCX plugin - Table becomes uneditable when only the header row remains (new rows cannot be added) - Extra bullet points added when pasting content from the Froala changelog page (Firefox only) - Toolbar dropdown position does not adjust to the available viewport space - Font style and size changes apply only to the first lines with `htmlUntouched: true` after pasting from Word or Outlook - A page break cannot reliably be dragged or deleted without selecting it (Page Break plugin) [Download 5.2.0 on GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor/releases/tag/v5.2.0) ## 5.1.0 (Apr 1, 2026) ### New and Improved - AI Assist plugin ### Fixed - Font size inconsistency in numbered list selection, ignoring the last empty list item - Decrease indent not working on ordered list - Clicking image caption scrolls to top of editor - Issue with `enter: FroalaEditor.ENTER_BR` and `
    ` - Table properties and cell properties popups display incorrectly in the dark theme - Backspace deletes character and the current line - Accessibility issue with the insert video popup - Paragraph text wraps around table when table alignment is set to `Left` - Accessibility issue on table cell properties - Toolbar popover buttons not working on iPad (Safari) - Image caption partially hidden if user inserts link to image - Missing translations in all languages - Incorrect edit popup positioning with sticky toolbar in scrollable container - Image disappears when dragging and dropping mixed content (image + text) pasted from external sources - Editor steals focus when `fontSizeDefaultSelection` or `htmlUntouched` is enabled - The Advanced Edit button can't be removed - Image disappears after updating link text on a captioned image link - `paste.afterCleanup` event triggered unexpectedly when moving/dragging a table inside the editor - Strings in dropdown lists are not localized [Download 5.1.0 on GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor/releases/tag/v5.1.0) ## 5.0.1 (Feb 18, 2026) ### Fixed - Vertical cell split propagates incorrectly to adjacent cells after inserting a row above in a table - Accidental vertical cell resizing triggered by a simple click on the cell border - Accessibility issue, aXe found missing labels on the style options menu icon - Image popup appears behind the editor and is not displayed on top - Selection highlight appears over the font list popup in iOS mobile view - Sub-bullets convert to numbered lists and the font becomes inconsistent after using Clean on Word paste - An extra “.” character is added when toggling Code View with a `

pages.title: Activation
pages.markdown:
# Activation Pass your license key to the editor as the `key` option. ## Get Your Key Once you [purchase a license](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/pricing/), use the keys sent to the email address you bought it with, or ask [support@froala.com](mailto:support@froala.com) for them. The [free trial](https://froala.com/wysiwyg_editor-download/) uses a trial key, which goes in the same option. ## Add the Key The key is a string. Each framework wrapper passes it to the editor with the rest of the options. **React** ```jsx import FroalaEditorComponent from 'react-froala-wysiwyg'; const config = { key: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY' }; export default function Editor() { return ; } ``` [React guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/react/) **TypeScript** ```ts import FroalaEditor, { type FroalaOptions } from 'froala-editor'; const config: Partial = { key: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY' }; new FroalaEditor('#editor', config); ``` [All options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/) **Vue** ```vue ``` [Vue guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/vue-js-3/) **Angular** ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { FroalaEditorModule, FroalaViewModule } from 'angular-froala-wysiwyg'; @Component({ selector: 'app-editor', standalone: true, imports: [FroalaEditorModule, FroalaViewModule], template: '
' }) export class EditorComponent { options = { key: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY' }; model = ''; } ``` [Angular guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/angular/) **JavaScript** ```js new FroalaEditor('#editor', { key: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY' }); ``` [Installation](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/) The editor no longer has a jQuery plugin, so `$(selector).froalaEditor()` isn't defined. Start it with `new FroalaEditor(selector, options)`, which needs no jQuery. ## What the editor shows The notice sits next to the "Powered by Froala" line, and the same text appears once in the browser console. It looks the same on localhost and on a public site. | Key | Notice | |---|---| | No key | The license key for Froala Editor is missing. To evaluate, use the trial key. To buy a license, go to froala.com. | | Trial key | You are using a 30-day trial version of Froala Editor, which is not for production use. Buy a license at froala.com. | | Invalid key | The license key for Froala Editor is invalid. Make sure to use the trial key or buy a license. | | Expired key | The license key for Froala Editor expired, please renew at froala.com or contact our sales team. | | Valid key | No notice. | - A term key keeps a clean editor for 15 days after it expires. After that it shows the expired notice. - An expired key shows the same notice on localhost and on a hosted site. - The editor checks that its notice stays visible, so do not hide it with CSS. These rules apply from Froala 5.6.0. Froala 5.5.0 and older show a red unlicensed banner on hosted sites, and only bold, italic and underline work there without a key. ## Other Integrations Every integration takes the key with its other options. Its README shows where they go. - [React README](https://github.com/froala/react-froala-wysiwyg#config) - [Vue README](https://github.com/froala/vue-froala-wysiwyg#options) - [Angular README](https://github.com/froala/angular-froala-wysiwyg#options) - [Aurelia README](https://github.com/froala/aurelia-froala-editor#options) - [Sencha Ext JS guide](https://docs.sencha.com/extjs/7.4.0/guides/components/froala.html#components-_-froala_-_specifying_a_froala_activation_key) - [AngularJS README](https://github.com/froala/angular-froala#options) The AngularJS wrapper, `angular-froala`, depends on an older major version of the editor in its latest npm release. For a current editor, use the Angular wrapper.

# Basic Concepts

## Custom Elements

# Custom Button

## Custom Button

The following section shows how to create a [custom button](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/getting-started/)for the editor.

1. First, define an icon for the button. FroalaEditor.DefineIcon('buttonIcon', { NAME: 'star', SVG_KEY: 'star' })
2. Define a button. FroalaEditor.RegisterCommand('myButton', {
3. Set the button title. title: 'My Button',
4. Specify the icon for the button. If this option is not specified, the button name is used. icon: 'buttonIcon',
5. Save the button action into undo stack. undo: true,
6. Focus inside the editor before the callback. focus: true,
7. Set `showOnMobile` to 'true' to show the button on mobile, which is the default, or to 'false' to hide it there. showOnMobile: true,
8. Add the following to refresh the buttons state after the callback. refreshAfterCallback: true,
9. Call a function when the button is hit.  
 The current context is the editor instance. callback: function () { console.log (this.html.get()); },
10. Call a function when the button state might have changed.  
 The current context is the editor instance. refresh: function ($btn) { console.log (this.selection.element()); }

Your final code should look like this.

```js
FroalaEditor.DefineIcon('buttonIcon', { NAME: 'star', SVG_KEY: 'star' })

FroalaEditor.RegisterCommand('myButton', {
  title: 'My Button',
  icon: 'buttonIcon',
  undo: true,
  focus: true,
  showOnMobile: true,
  refreshAfterCallback: true,
  callback: function () {
    console.log (this.html.get());
  },
  refresh: function ($btn) {
    console.log (this.selection.element());
  }
})
```

For a working example please refer to the [Custom Buttons Example](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/examples/custom-buttons/) or the [Custom Image Button Example](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/examples/custom-image-button/)

Once a command is defined it can be included in any option that is using buttons, such as `imageAltButtons`, `imageEditButtons`, `imageInsertButtons`, `imageSizeButtons`, `linkEditButtons`, `linkInsertButtons`, `tableColorsButtons`, `tableEditButtons`, `tableInsertButtons`, `toolbarButtons`, `toolbarButtonsMD`, `toolbarButtonsSM`, `toolbarButtonsXS`, `videoEditButtons`, `videoInsertButtons` or `videoSizeButtons`.

## Additional Resources

- [Creating Custom Buttons with React and Froala Editor](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/creating-custom-buttons-with-react-and-froala-editor/)
- [Custom Buttons with Froala in an Angular Application](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/custom-buttons-with-froala-in-an-angular-application/)

pages.markdown: # Image Manager The Image Manager lets users browse the images on your server, insert them and delete them. It needs two addresses on your server, one that lists the images and one that deletes an image. ## How It Works 1. The user picks Insert Image, then Browse. The editor sends one request to `imageManagerLoadURL` for the whole list. 2. Your server answers with a JSON array of images. The manager shows their thumbnails, `imageManagerPageSize` at a time, and adds more as the user scrolls. 3. The user clicks an image, and the editor inserts it. 4. The user deletes an image and confirms. The editor sends a request to `imageManagerDeleteURL`, and your server deletes the file. Until you set these options, the manager lists sample images from Froala's server (`https://i.froala.com/load-files`), and deleting an image fails with error 22, because there is no delete address. ## Set Up the Editor `froala_editor.pkgd.min.js` already has the Image Manager. With the core editor, load the Image plugin and then the Image Manager plugin, with their stylesheets. Loaded without the Image plugin, the Image Manager stops with an error. ```html ``` Then set the two addresses, and the other options you need. ```js new FroalaEditor('#editor', { // The request that lists the images. imageManagerLoadURL: '/load_images', imageManagerLoadMethod: 'GET', imageManagerLoadParams: { user_id: 4219762 }, // The request that deletes an image. imageManagerDeleteURL: '/delete_image', imageManagerDeleteMethod: 'POST', imageManagerDeleteParams: { user_id: 4219762 }, // How the list is shown. imageManagerPageSize: 20, imageManagerScrollOffset: 10, imageManagerPreloader: '/images/loader.gif', events: { 'imageManager.imagesLoaded': function (data) { // The list arrived. data is your server's response, as text. }, 'imageManager.imageLoaded': function ($img) { // One thumbnail loaded in the manager. }, 'imageManager.beforeDeleteImage': function ($img) { // The user confirmed a delete. Return false to keep the image. }, 'imageManager.imageDeleted': function (data) { // Your server deleted the image. data is its response. }, 'imageManager.error': function (error, response) { console.log(error.code, error.message, response); } } }); ``` | Option | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | [`imageManagerLoadURL`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerLoadURL) | `'https://i.froala.com/load-files'` | The address that lists the images. | | [`imageManagerLoadMethod`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerLoadMethod) | `'get'` | The HTTP method of the list request. | | [`imageManagerLoadParams`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerLoadParams) | `{}` | More parameters for the list request. With GET, they go in the query string. | | [`imageManagerDeleteURL`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerDeleteURL) | `''` | The address that deletes an image. | | [`imageManagerDeleteMethod`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerDeleteMethod) | `'post'` | The HTTP method of the delete request. | | [`imageManagerDeleteParams`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerDeleteParams) | `{}` | More parameters for the delete request. | | [`imageManagerPageSize`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerPageSize) | `12` | How many images the manager adds at a time. | | [`imageManagerScrollOffset`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerScrollOffset) | `20` | How close to the bottom, in pixels, the user scrolls before more images appear. | | [`imageManagerPreloader`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerPreloader) | `null` | An image to show while the list loads, in place of the Loading text. | | [`imageManagerToggleTags`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#imageManagerToggleTags) | `true` | Whether the user can show and hide the tag filter. | Both requests send `requestHeaders`, and cookies when `requestWithCredentials` is `true`, so your server can check who is asking. ## The List Your Server Returns Answer the list request with a JSON array, one object per image. ```json [ { "url": "https://example.com/images/photo1.jpg", "thumb": "https://example.com/thumbs/photo1.jpg", "tag": "flower", "name": "Photo 1", "id": "103454285" }, { "url": "https://example.com/images/photo2.jpg", "thumb": "https://example.com/thumbs/photo2.jpg", "tag": "sport,outdoor" } ] ``` | Field | Needed | What the editor does with it | | --- | --- | --- | | `url` | Yes | The image it inserts. The inserted image keeps it in `data-url` too. | | `thumb` | Recommended | The image the manager shows. Without it, the manager loads the full image and fires error 14. | | `tag` | No | Adds a filter tag above the list. Separate several tags with commas. | | `name` | No | Becomes the image's `alt` text, and `data-name`. | | Any other field | No | Becomes a `data-` attribute of the same name, such as `data-id`. | The first image above is inserted like this. ```html ``` To report a problem, answer with an HTTP error status. The editor fires `imageManager.error` with code 11 and your response. A response that can't be parsed fires code 13. An object in place of the array, such as one with an `error` field, only shows an empty manager. ## The Delete Request When the user deletes an image and confirms, the editor fires `imageManager.beforeDeleteImage`, then sends these fields, form encoded, to `imageManagerDeleteURL`. | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | `src` | The address the manager shows, which is the `thumb` when the list has one. | | `data-url` | The full image's address, from `url`. | | `alt` and the other `data-` fields | The image's other list fields, such as `data-id`. | | Your parameters | Each key in `imageManagerDeleteParams`. | Delete the file, and its thumbnail, and answer with a success status. The editor then removes the image from the list and fires `imageManager.imageDeleted` with your response. An error status fires `imageManager.error` with code 21 and leaves the image in the list. ## Events and Errors Inside a handler, `this` is the editor. | Event | When it fires | | --- | --- | | [`imageManager.imagesLoaded(data)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#imageManager.imagesLoaded) | The list request succeeded. `data` is the response as text. | | [`imageManager.imageLoaded($img)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#imageManager.imageLoaded) | A thumbnail loaded in the manager. | | [`imageManager.beforeDeleteImage($img)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#imageManager.beforeDeleteImage) | The user confirmed a delete. Return `false` to cancel it. | | [`imageManager.imageDeleted(data)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#imageManager.imageDeleted) | The delete request succeeded. `data` is the response. | | [`imageManager.error(error, response)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#imageManager.error) | Something failed. `error` has a `code` and a `message`. | | Code | Message | | --- | --- | | 10 | Image cannot be loaded from the passed link. | | 11 | Error during load images request. | | 12 | Missing imageManagerLoadURL option. | | 13 | Parsing load response failed. | | 14 | Missing image thumb. | | 15 | Missing image URL. | | 21 | Error during delete image request. | | 22 | Missing imageManagerDeleteURL option. | ## Server Code Each Froala server SDK has a guide to listing a folder of images for the manager and deleting one. - [.NET SDK Image Manager](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/dotnet/image-manager/) - [Java SDK Image Manager](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/java/image-manager/) - [Node.js SDK Image Manager](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/nodejs/image-manager/) - [PHP SDK Image Manager](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/php/image-manager/) - [Python SDK Image Manager](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/python/image-manager/) - [Ruby SDK Image Manager](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/ruby/image-manager/)

pages.markdown:
# Save Froala Editor Content Inside a Form

## Save inside FORM

To store the content of the editor on the server side save the content inside a FORM. Initialize the editor on a `textarea` inside a form, then send the content to the server as value of `textarea`.

### *Initialize the editor*

```html
<form action="save" method="POST">
  <textarea name="editor_content" id="myEditor"></textarea>
  <button>Submit</button>
</form>

<script>
  new FroalaEditor('#myEditor', {toolbarInline: false})
</script>
```

### *Receive request on the server*

The FORM sends the content in the `editor_content` parameter of the request (which is the name of the textarea), the server processes the request and saves the data in the DB.

In PHP, for the code above you would get the rich text editor's content in `$_POST['editor_content']` variable.

pages.markdown:
# Building an LMS Course Creation Page with Froala Course authors require different editing tools depending on what they are creating. When building a new course in a [learning management systems](https://froala.com/solutions/learning-management/), they are typically guided through a page of content blocks, each with a distinct instructional purpose. These may include videos, texts, assignments, discussions, and announcements blocks. Froala’s rich-text editor can be configured differently for each one, giving authors exactly the right tools at the right moment. With more than [240 configuration options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/), Froala can be tailored to match the workflow of each block type. This guide covers core learning blocks first, then specialized blocks, followed by shared configuration patterns, implementation guidance, and a complete interactive example that brings all configurations together in a practical LMS course builder. ## Why Choose Froala for LMS Platforms? For product managers and LMS decision-makers, Froala delivers significant business value beyond its technical features. It empowers non-technical authors to build engaging content without writing code, standardizes course design across modules, and drastically reduces support tickets related to formatting problems. By offering a tailored and reliable editing experience, institutions can elevate the quality of their educational materials while accelerating course creation. ## Core LMS Block Configurations The guide starts with the most common authoring blocks used to create lessons, assessments, and learner interactions. These configurations focus on providing course creators with the right tools for the job without overwhelming the editing experience. ### Video Block Authors can use this block to visually explain their lessons. Configure Froala with a minimal toolbar focused on media embedding. Enable video upload or embed options, allow pasting from popular video platforms, and enable Filestack plugin for advanced video upload and transformation. ```js new FroalaEditor('#video-block',{ pluginsEnabled: ['video', 'image', 'link', 'filestack', 'filesManager', 'file'], toolbarButtons: ["insertLink", "insertImage", "insertVideo", "openFilePickerVideo"], videoUpload: true, videoAllowedProviders: ["youtube", "vimeo", "dailymotion"], videoDefaultWidth: 0, videoMaxSize: 1024 * 1024 * 15, videoResponsive: true, videoAllowedTypes: [ 'mp4', 'webm' ], videoUploadURL: '/upload_video', filestackOptions: { filestackAPI: '***', pickerOptions: { fromSources: [ 'local_file_system', 'imagesearch', 'url', 'googledrive', 'facebook', ], }, }, placeholderText: "Embed or upload your course video here..." }); ``` ### Details Block Authors can use this block to enter the full course details. Use a full rich-text toolbar with headings, bold, italics, lists, tables, links, and alignment tools. This setup is ideal for lesson explanations, summaries, and reading content, where formatting flexibility improves readability. Creators can also use this block for learning objectives, such as listing course goals and measurable outcomes at the start of a module, and for FAQs that clearly organize common learner questions. ```js new FroalaEditor('#text-block',{ toolbarButtons: ['undo', 'redo', '|', 'paragraphFormat', '|', 'fontSize', '|', 'bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'strikeThrough', 'textColor', '|', 'insertLink', 'insertImage', 'insertTable', '|', 'alignLeft', 'alignCenter', 'alignRight', 'alignJustify', 'formatUL', 'formatOL', 'outdent', 'indent', '|', 'html'], placeholderText: 'Write your lesson content here...', heightMin: 300, }); ``` ### Assignment Block Set up Froala to support detailed instructions, file references, due date formatting, and rubric descriptions. Toolbar options, such as lists, tables, attachments integration, and links, help course creators clearly define expectations. ```js new FroalaEditor('#assignment-block',{ toolbarButtons: ['undo', 'redo', '|', 'paragraphFormat', '|', 'bold', 'italic', 'underline', '|', 'insertLink', 'insertTable', 'insertFile', '|', 'align', 'formatUL', 'formatOL'], fileUpload: true, fileAllowedTypes: ['application/pdf', 'application/msword'], placeholderText: 'Describe the assignment instructions, rubric, and deadlines...', }); ``` ### Discussion Block Use a lighter configuration that encourages fast posting and interactions. It includes basic text styling, quotes, emojis where supported, and link insertion, so instructors can create engaging discussion prompts while maintaining a clean editing experience. ```js new FroalaEditor('#discussion-block', { toolbarButtons: ['undo', 'redo', '|', 'bold', 'italic', '|', 'insertLink', '|', 'emoticons', '|', 'quote'], placeholderText: 'Start a discussion prompt or reply here...', heightMin: 100, charCounterCount: true, charCounterMax: 1000 }); ``` ### Announcement Block Configure Froala with a clean, focused toolbar to write clear and concise announcements. It supports basic formatting, links, and emojis so that instructors can share updates in a friendly, readable way. Use Froala’s [Paragraph Styles feature](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/examples/paragraph-styles/) to enable authors quickly apply predefined formatting to entire paragraphs without manually changing individual text properties. ```js new FroalaEditor('#announcement-block',{ toolbarButtons: [ 'undo', 'redo', '|', 'paragraphFormat', '|', 'bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'paragraphStyle', '|', 'insertLink', '|', 'emoticons', '|', 'alignLeft', 'alignCenter', ], paragraphStyles: { new_course: 'New Course', update: 'Important Update' }, placeholderText: 'Write your course announcement...', wordCounterMax: 1500, }); ``` ## Common Features Across LMS Blocks Although each LMS block benefits from a tailored toolbar and feature set, several Froala capabilities are valuable across nearly all the block types. For example. ### AI Assist Froala AI Assist fits naturally into any block by helping course creators draft lesson text, improve clarity, rephrase instructions, summarize long content, and generate ideas for quizzes, announcements, or discussion prompts. This is especially useful when building courses quickly, maintaining a consistent tone across modules, or refining educational content for better learner understanding and engagement. For example, an instructor writing a lesson introduction can use AI Assist to expand a short outline into a polished explanation, whereas a quiz author can generate question ideas directly from the lesson content. In a production environment, AI features require a server setup to secure the AI model API code. [Here is an example of setting up an AI assist.](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/froala-deepseek-ai-wordpress-setup/) ```js { // AI Assist configuration aiSupplementalTermsAccepted: true, aiAssistRequest: sendDataToAI, // Event handlers events: { 'initialized': function () { console.log('Froala Editor initialized with AI Assist'); }, 'aiAssist.afterInsert': function () { console.error('AI response is ready.'); } } } ``` ### Scientific Content For STEM course creation, configure Froala with MathType integration so that instructors can write and embed mathematical equations, scientific notation, and complex formulas naturally within their content. Pairing this with code snippets and image insertion makes the block especially useful for technical lessons, lab documentation, and other science- or engineering-focused materials. Here is a guide for [integrating Froala with MathType](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/simple-integration-guide-adding-math-equations-and-chemistry-formulas-to-froala-editor/) to enable scientific content editing. ### Import from Word Froala enable course creators to [upload Word documents (.docx)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/import-from-word-plugin/) directly into any block. This reduce manual content entry time. ```js {     importFromWordMaxFileSize: 1 * 1024 * 1024, importFromWordFileTypesAllowed: ['docx'], } ``` ### Export to Word Creators can download their [course content as formatted Word documents](https://froala.com/blog/editor/save-time-reduce-rework-froalas-export-to-word-in-action/). This is especially useful for offline reviews, stakeholder approval, and compliance documentation. ```js { wordExportFileName: "myCourseName", } ``` ### Export to PDF Authors can [generate PDF versions of their course content](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/a-step-by-step-guide-to-export-froala-wysiwyg-editor-to-pdf/) for distribution, printing, and archival purposes. PDF export preserves the formatting, images, and layout while providing a portable, shareable format that works across devices. ### Code Snippet Use [Froala’s Code Snippet plugin](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/code-snippet-plugin/) tailored for technical courses that require formatted code. The code view, monospace font support, and minimal formatting were enabled so that instructors could insert and label code examples cleanly. ### Advanced File Management You can use the Filestack plugin to easily integrate powerful file uploading and management capabilities into your web application. The [Filestack Plugin](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/filestack-plugin/) provides a way to handle file uploads and transformations through a simple and intuitive user interface. ## Security, Accessibility & UX Before shipping these configurations, address security, accessibility, and UX edge cases so that your LMS is safe, usable, and reliable in production. ### Security - Sanitize HTML server-side (never trust client-side filters). Enable Froala’s sanitize, and run server validation to remove disallowed tags/attributes. - Restrict uploads. Enforce allowed MIME types and maximum file size in both client and server codes. For example, reject uploads > 10 MB and require a content type match. - Upload endpoints are protected with authentication and CSRF protection. Add per-request signed headers if your storage service supports this. - Virus/AV scanning. Integrate a scanning step on uploaded files before making them publicly available. [Filestack can help you automatically detect viruses and malware](https://froala.com/blog/general/add-virus-detection-html-editor-software/) before serving them to users. Ensure logging, alerting, and regular security reviews to maintain infrastructure integrity and its resilience. ### Accessibility - Provide sufficient color contrast for callouts and text color/background color choices. - Ensure that MathType and code blocks have accessible fallbacks (alt text for images, MathML, or LaTeX fallback for screen readers when possible). - Testing with screen readers and keyboard-only navigation early. ### UX & Reliability - Autosave. [Set up autosave with periodic backups](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/save-plugin/) to prevent data loss during network interruptions or unexpected browser crashes in your LMS environment. This can be easily performed using the Save plugin. - Offline resilience. Allow draft composition offline and queue uploads when the connection returns. - Mobile/compact toolbars. Provide a simplified toolbar for small screens to avoid overflow issues. Froala offer [dedicated configuration for touch interfaces](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/unlock-the-power-of-customizable-toolbars-with-froala/), making content creation accessible across devices and screen sizes without sacrificing functionality. - Error handling. [Utilize Froala events](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/) to display clear error messages and preserve content on failure. ### Developer Ergonomics SCORM and LTI Compatibility. Because Froala produces clean, semantic HTML, the resulting content can easily be packaged into SCORM modules or served via LTI integrations without breaking layouts or introducing invalid markup. ## Interactive Example. LMS Block Configuration in Action This example ties the article together by demonstrating how multiple Froala block configurations can coexist on a single course creation page. Each block is initialized independently with its own tailored toolbar, performance settings, and feature set. To demonstrate how these Froala configurations work in a real LMS environment, here is a complete working example with HTML and JavaScript that lets you switch between different block types and see each editor initialized with its specific configuration. ### HTML Structure The interface consists of a sidebar menu with buttons for each block type and a main editing area. When a course creator clicks a menu button, a new editor instance is dynamically added to the form. The Froala CSS is loaded from CDN, and custom paragraph styles for announcements (new course and important update) are defined with distinct visual styling to help instructors quickly identify announcement types. ```html
``` ### JavaScript Configuration The configuration object centralizes all editor settings, with a common section for shared options (Word import/export, AI Assist) and block-specific sections for each content type. Each block type has a tailored toolbar and feature set. When a course creator clicks a menu button, the script generates a unique ID for each new editor, creates a textarea element within the form, and initializes a Froala instance by merging the common configuration with the block-specific settings. The submit button is enabled once the first block is added, allowing creators to build multi-block courses by repeatedly clicking menu buttons. ```html ``` Together, these capabilities confirm that Froala is not just a text editor, it is a fully configurable content authoring platform that adapts to the structure and requirements of any LMS workflow. ### Still need another block Type? The Froala Editor has a powerful API that allows, as you see above, easy customization of the editor to perform different functions. Discover more than [240 options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/), +[100 events](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/), and [+220 methods](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/) and start customizing it to your functionality. Need more? Froala is easily extended by creating custom [plugins](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/custom/plugin/), [buttons](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/custom/button/), [pop-ups](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/custom/popup/), and [dropdown menus](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/custom/dropdown/). Want to style the Froala Editor to your brand style? You can customize the Froala user interface from [editing icons](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/custom/icon/) to completely using another [color theme](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/examples/color-themes/). ### Displaying The Page Content After creating a course and wants to display its content to the users, remember to follow the final step mentioned on the [get started](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/) page. 1. Include the froala style sheet ```html ``` 1. Make sure that you put the edited content inside an element that has the class fr-view. ```html
``` ## What do customers say about Froala Editor? It feels like we tried every editor on the market before discovering Froala! We haven’t looked back since. # Development Frameworks

Guides for using the editor in front-end frameworks, back-end frameworks and CMSs, each with the package it installs. Every integration but Sencha's is in Froala's GitHub organization, and some were started by people who use the editor.

## Front-end Frameworks

The npm wrappers depend on `froala-editor`. Install both, as each guide shows, and keep them at the same version.

| Framework | Package | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [React](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/react/) | `react-froala-wysiwyg` | A component for React 0.14 to 19. |
| [Angular](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/angular/) | `angular-froala-wysiwyg` | Directives for Angular 19 and later. |
| [Vue](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/vue-js-3/) | `vue-froala-wysiwyg` | A component for Vue 3.2 and later. |
| [Svelte](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/svelte/) | `svelte-froala-wysiwyg` | A component for Svelte 5. |
| [Gatsby](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/gatsby/) | `react-froala-wysiwyg` | The React component, loaded in the browser. |
| [Ionic](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/ionic/) | `angular-froala-wysiwyg` | The Angular directives, in an Ionic Angular app. |
| [Ember](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/ember/) | `ember-froala-editor` | An addon for Ember 3.20 and later. Its latest release depends on an older major version of the editor. |
| [Aurelia](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/aurelia/) | `aurelia-froala-editor` | A custom element for Aurelia 1. |
| [Knockout](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/knockout/) | `knockout-froala` | Knockout bindings for the editor. |
| [Meteor](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/meteor/) | `froala:editor` | An Atmosphere package with the editor's files. |
| [Sencha Ext JS](https://docs.sencha.com/extjs/7.4.0/guides/components/froala.html) | `@sencha/ext-froala-editor` | Sencha's own component for the Ext JS Modern toolkit, from Sencha's npm registry, documented by Sencha. |

## Back-end Frameworks and CMSs

These packages bring the editor's files with them and add the editor to the framework's forms or admin.

| Framework | Package | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Django](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/django/) | `django-froala-editor`, on PyPI | A model field and a form widget, with upload views. |
| [Ruby on Rails](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/rails/) | `wysiwyg-rails`, a gem | The editor's files in the asset pipeline, for Rails 3.2.7 up to Rails 8. |
| [Symfony](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/symfony/) | `kms/froala-editor-bundle`, on Composer | A form type and upload routes. Its latest release supports Symfony 4.4 and 5. |
| [Yii](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/yii/) | `froala/yii2-froala-editor`, on Composer | A widget for Yii 2. |
| [CakePHP](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/cakephp/) | `froala/wysiwyg-cake`, on Composer | A plugin and view helper for CakePHP 3. |
| [Craft CMS](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/craft-cms/) | `froala/craft-froala-wysiwyg`, on Composer | A rich text field for Craft CMS 3. |
| [WordPress](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/wordpress/) | A plugin, from GitHub | Takes the classic editor's place in the admin, and starts the editor on the front end. |

## Server SDKs

For image and file uploads in any back end, the server SDKs and server guides cover the code on your side.

- [Server Integrations](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/server-integrations/)

Clone this repo or download the zip. 2. Run `bower install` or Download the editor from [https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/) 3. Load Froala WYSIWYG editor (and all desired plugins) and the angular-froala files into your project. - src/angular-froala.js ## Update editor With npm: ``` npm update froala-editor ``` With bower: ``` bower install froala-wysiwyg-editor ``` ## Usage 1. Add the `froala` dependency to your Angular project. example: - `angular.module('myApp', ['froala'])` 2. Create a textarea with the froala directive in your view and give it a model, where `myHtml` is a variable on `$scope`. - `` ### Options **Setting Defaults**: to set defaults for the editor pass a config object to angular.value with the key `froalaConfig` like this: ``` angular.module('myApp', ['froala']). value('froalaConfig', { toolbarInline: false, placeholderText: 'Enter Text Here' }); ``` **From the Controller**: to set options from the controller, create an options object on scope and simply pass it to the froala directive. example: _app.js_ ``` function myCtrl($scope){ $scope.myHtml = "

Hello World

" $scope.froalaOptions = { toolbarButtons : ["bold", "italic", "underline", "|", "align", "formatOL", "formatUL"] } } ``` _view.html_ ``` ``` You can pass any existing Froala option. Consult the [Froala documentation](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options) to view the list of all the available options. #### Directive Specific Option The _angular-froala_ directive exposes the following additional option: - **immediateAngularModelUpdate**: (default: false) This option synchronizes the angular model as soon as a key is released in the editor. Note that it may affect performances. ### Methods To use the methods available, access the editor instance from your froalaOptions object `$scope.options.froalaEditor(method)` and use it as described in the [method docs](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods). example: ``` function myCtrl($scope){ $scope.myHtml = ""; $scope.froalaOptions = { toolbarButtons : ["bold", "italic", "underline", "|", "align", "formatOL", "formatUL"], events: { 'froalaEditor.initialized': function () { // Use the methods like this. $scope.froalaOptions.froalaEditor('selection.get'); } } } } ``` ### Events Events can be passed in with the options, with a key events and object where the key is the event name and the value is the callback function. #### Attribute _app.js_ ``` $scope.froalaOptions = { placeholder: "Edit Me", events : { 'froalaEditor.focus' : function(e, editor) { /* ... */ } } } ``` ### Special tags You can also use the editor on **img**, **button**, **input** and **a** tags: ``` ``` The model must be an object containing the attributes for your special tags. Example: ``` $scope.imgObj = { src: 'path/to/image.jpg' }; ``` The ng-model will change as the attributes change during usage. - Ng-model can contain a special attribute named **innerHTML** which inserts innerHTML in the element: If you are using 'button' tag, you can specify the button text like this: ``` $scope.buttonObj = { innerHTML: 'Button text' }; ``` As the button text is modified by the editor, the **innerHTML** attribute from buttonObj model will be modified too. #### Specific option for special tags - **angularIgnoreAttrs**: (default: null) This option is an array of attributes that you want to ignore when the editor updates the ng-model: ``` $scope.inputOptions = { angularIgnoreAttrs: ['class', 'ng-model', 'id'] }; ``` ### Manual Instantiation Sometimes you want to control when the Froala Editor will be instantiated. The directive includes a **froala-init** attributes which will provide you with the controls required to initialize and close the editor. ```
``` Where _MyControllerFunction_ is the name of a function in your controller which will receive an object with different methods to control the editor initialization process. It is primordial that the name of the parameter be _initControls_ otherwise your function will not receive the controls. The object received by the function will contain the following methods: - **initialize**: Call this method to initialize the Froala Editor - **destroy**: Call this method to destroy the Froala Editor - **getEditor**: Call this method to retrieve the editor that was created. This method will return _null_ if the editor was not yet created Checkout the demo file to see a working example. To display content created with the froala editor use the froala-view directive. if `myHtml` is your model, then the following will render your content. ```
``` If you are using the old `ng-bind-html` that will continue to work however it still requires froala-sanitize.js to be used and not all of froala is supported with it. The updated directive does **not** require froala-sanitize. Congrats all is done!

`, }) export class AppComponent implements OnInit{ ngOnInit () { $.FroalaEditor.DefineIcon('alert', {NAME: 'info'}); $.FroalaEditor.RegisterCommand('alert', { title: 'Hello', focus: false, undo: false, refreshAfterCallback: false, callback: () => { alert('Hello!', this); } }); } public options: Object = { charCounterCount: true, toolbarButtons: ['bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'paragraphFormat','alert'], toolbarButtonsXS: ['bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'paragraphFormat','alert'], toolbarButtonsSM: ['bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'paragraphFormat','alert'], toolbarButtonsMD: ['bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'paragraphFormat','alert'], }; } ``` ### Special tags You can also use the editor on **img**, **button**, **input** and **a** tags: ``` ``` The model must be an object containing the attributes for your special tags. For example: ``` public imgObj: Object = { src: 'path/to/image.jpg' }; ``` The froalaModel will change as the attributes change during usage. froalaModel can contain a special attribute named **innerHTML** which inserts innerHTML in the element: If you are using 'button' tag, you can specify the button text like this: ``` public buttonModel: Object = { innerHTML: 'Click Me' }; ``` As the button text is modified by the editor, the **innerHTML** attribute from buttonModel model will be modified too. ### Specific option for special tags **angularIgnoreAttrs**: (default: null) This option is an array of attributes that you want to ignore when the editor updates the froalaModel: ``` public inputOptions: Object = { angularIgnoreAttrs: ['class', 'id'] }; ``` ## Manual Initialization Gets the functionality to operate on the editor: create, destroy and get editor instance. Use it if you want to manually initialize the editor. `(froalaInit)="initialize($event)"` Where `initialize` is the name of a function in your component which will receive an object with different methods to control the editor initialization process. ``` public initialize(initControls) { this.initControls = initControls; this.deleteAll = function() { this.initControls.getEditor()('html.set', ''); }; } ``` The object received by the function will contain the following methods: - **initialize**: Call this method to initialize the Froala Editor - **destroy**: Call this method to destroy the Froala Editor - **getEditor**: Call this method to retrieve the editor that was created. This method will return _null_ if the editor was not yet created ## Displaying HTML To display content created with the froala editor use the froalaView directive. `[froalaView]="editorContent"` ```

Its source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/froala/aurelia-froala-editor). ## Installation ```shell npm install froala-editor aurelia-froala-editor ``` The wrapper depends on the exact `froala-editor` version it was released with and on `aurelia-framework` 1, so keep the editor and the wrapper at the same version. ### Update Update both packages together. ```shell npm install froala-editor@latest aurelia-froala-editor@latest ``` ## Add the Editor Register the plugin in `src/main.js` or `src/main.ts`, then require the styles and add the element in a template. The bundler needs a few lines more. **Aurelia CLI** ```js // src/main.js aurelia.use.plugin('aurelia-froala-editor'); ``` ```html ``` With the CLI's bundler, set the text plugin's `stub` to `false` in `aurelia_project/aurelia.json`, so the CSS is bundled. ```json "loader": { "type": "require", "configTarget": "vendor-bundle.js", "includeBundleMetadataInConfig": "auto", "plugins": [ { "name": "text", "extensions": [".html", ".css"], "stub": false } ] } ``` Then add the wrapper to the `dependencies` of `vendor-bundle.js` in the same file. ```json { "name": "aurelia-froala-editor", "path": "../node_modules/aurelia-froala-editor/dist/amd", "main": "index", "resources": ["froala-editor.js", "froala-editor.html"], "deps": ["froala-editor"] } ``` ```shell au run --watch ``` **Webpack** ```js // src/main.js import { PLATFORM } from 'aurelia-pal'; import 'froala-editor/js/froala_editor.pkgd.min.js'; aurelia.use.plugin(PLATFORM.moduleName('aurelia-froala-editor')); ``` ```html ``` In `webpack.config.js`, tell the Aurelia plugin about the element's module. ```js const { AureliaPlugin, ModuleDependenciesPlugin } = require('aurelia-webpack-plugin'); plugins: [ new AureliaPlugin(), new ModuleDependenciesPlugin({ 'aurelia-froala-editor': ['./froala-editor'] }) ] ``` ```shell npm run start ``` The README advises Webpack for the third-party plugins, such as Font Awesome, Spell Checker, Embedly and TUI image editing. ## Usage | Attribute | What it does | | --- | --- | | `value` | The content, as an HTML string. Bind it with `value.two-way`. | | `config` | The editor's options. | | `event-handlers` | The editor's events, keyed by event name. | ### Value The element writes the editor's HTML to `value` when the content changes and when the editor loses focus. A `config` on the element replaces these, it doesn't add to them. ```js aurelia.use.plugin('aurelia-froala-editor', config => { config.options({ toolbarInline: true }); }); ``` ### Events Pass [event](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/) handlers with `event-handlers.bind`, not in `config`, because the element replaces `config.events` with its own. Unlike the other wrappers, a handler here runs with your view-model as `this` and gets the event's arguments. ```html ``` ```js export class App { content = '

Hello from Froala

# CakePHP

[GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-cake)

The plugin is for CakePHP 3 only. Its latest release requires `cakephp/cakephp >=3.3.2 <4.0.0`, so a CakePHP 4 or 5 app can't install it. On Packagist the latest release is v5.2.0, from May 2026, although the GitHub repository has tags up to v5.5.0. For CakePHP 2 there is a separate plugin, [wysiwyg-cake2](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-cake2). In a CakePHP 4 or 5 app, load `froala-editor` yourself and start it on your textarea, as the [Installation guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/) shows.

## About

Place [Froala Editor](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/) in a plugin to keep it separate from a themed view, the regular webroot, or the app in general, this makes easier to perform updates and follows the idea of keeping the code clean and modular.

## Installation

To install the Froala Editor you you have the following options.

- Clone the git repository. git clone https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-cake.git plugins/Froala
- If your CakePHP application is setup as a git repository, you can add it as a submodule. git submodule add https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-cake.git plugins/Froala
- Or open terminal/command prompt (windows) and run `composer require froala/wysiwyg-cake`.
- Alternatively, you can download an archive from the [master branch on Github](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-cake/archive/master.zip) and extract the contents to `plugins/Froala`.

Make sure that you load the plugin routes by adding to your bootstrap file(bootstrap.php) in config folder.

`Plugin::loadAll(); or  Plugin::load('Froala');` This will load all plugins at once or only the Froala plugin.

## Usage

The Froala helper allows you to use php and CakePHP conventions to generate the configuration for Froala and also allows you to load configs.

```php
// Loads Froala Editor javascript also loads all the plugins and css for the plugins
<?= $this->Froala->plugin();?>

// Will target one specific html selector on which the editor will be init.
// Second paramenter can be an object/array of options that the Froala Editor takes.

<?= $this->Froala->editor('#froala', array('option' => value));?>
```

## How to use the helper

Since CakePHP 3.0 it is necessary to activate the plugin in your application.

To activate it edit `config/bootstrap.php` and add the line `Plugin::load('Froala');` at the bottom. If you already have `Plugin::loadAll();` to auto-load all plugins then you may skip this step.

To use it load it in the controller.

1. Open AppController.php (your project/src/controller/AppController) Declare variable public $helpers = array('Froala.Froala'); class AppController extends Controller { ... public $helpers = array('Froala.Froala'); ... }
2. In the view page (template) add `<?= $this->Froala->editor('#froala-editor');?>` This is a simple init example with no options for the Froala Editor. Include the below statement in your view template to integrate the plugins in your editor$this->Froala->plugin(); $this->Froala->editor('selector');This will instruct Froala to convert the matched element on the page to Froala editor.

Refer to [Froala configuration options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/) for a complete list of available options.

## Default options

If you want a quick way to configure default values for all the Froala Editors of an application, you could use the 'Froala.editorOptions' configuration.

Here is an example of a line you could have in `bootstrap.php`.

```php
Configure::write('Froala.editorOptions', array('height' => '300px'));
```

It will make all editors to have a 300px height. You may want to override this value for a single editor. To do so, just pass the option to the editor() method and it will override the default value.

## Usage examples

Example of init using array of options

```php
// '#comment'  Represents the html element selector.
// 'array()'   Represents the list of options that are passed to the editor.

$this->Froala->editor('#comment', array(
    'heightMin' => '200px',
    'heightMax' => '400px'
));
```

## Requirements

- PHP 5.5.9 or later
- CakePHP 3.3.2 or later, before CakePHP 4

## Additional Resources

- [How To Use WYSIWYG Editor In PHP](https://froala.com/blog/editor/how-to-use-wysiwyg-editor-in-php/)
- [Types of JavaScript WYSIWYG Editors](https://froala.com/blog/editor/the-anatomy-of-a-great-html-editor-online/)
- [6 Server Side Frameworks With Easy WYSIWYG Editor Integration](https://froala.com/blog/general/6-server-side-frameworks-with-wysiwyg-editor-integration/)

# Craft CMS

[GitHub](https://github.com/froala/Craft-3-Froala-WYSIWYG)

The plugin, `froala/craft-froala-wysiwyg`, is for Craft 3 only. It requires `craftcms/cms ^3.1`, so Craft 4 and 5 can't install it. The Craft Plugin Store lists version 5.5.0; on Packagist, where `composer require` looks, the latest release is 5.2.0, from May 2026, which installs editor 5.2.0. The plugin for Craft 2, `froala/craft-froala-editor`, last changed in 2019 and comes with editor 2.9.3.

## Known issue

Adding links to Craft Entries causing issues when you double click on the entry to link to. Just click once and use the "Select" button.

Sorry for the inconvience. We're working on these annoying issues. But we decided to release a new version because of some missing important other features (like saving links the Craft way).

## Installation

You have the following installation options.

### Composer installation

Go to your project directory, require the plugin with Composer, then tell Craft to install it.

```shell
cd /path/to/my-project
composer require froala/craft-froala-wysiwyg
./craft install/plugin froala-editor
```

### From the Plugin Store

Go to the Plugin Store in your project's Control Panel and search for "Froala". Then click the "Install" button in its window.

To enable the editor you need a license, you can get it at [froala.com](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/pricing/).

Once you have a license for your domain, you can enter the license key in the plugin settings.

## Features

- Ability to set your license key in plugin settings
- Ability to disable/enable editor plugins via settings
- Creating fields defined as Richtext Froala Editor
- Ability to pick a custom editor config per field, from JSON files in `config/froalaeditor/`
- Configuration of Craft Asset sources for image/file uploads
- Configuration of custom CSS file to be loaded relative from the site or from a plugin resource

# Django

`django-froala-editor` adds the editor to Django as a model field and a form widget, with image and file upload views. It ships the editor's files, and its source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/froala/django-froala-editor).

## Installation

```shell
pip install django-froala-editor
```

Each release bundles the editor of the same version in its static files, so updating the package updates the editor.

Add `froala_editor` to `INSTALLED_APPS` in `settings.py`, then add its URLs to your project's `urls.py`.

```python
from django.urls import include, path

urlpatterns = [
    # ... your other URL patterns
    path('froala_editor/', include('froala_editor.urls')),
]
```

The URLs turn on image and file upload. Without them, the editor turns both off, and images can still be added from a URL.

The package's upload views don't check who is uploading, so anyone who can reach the URLs can store files on your site. On a public site, protect them, for example by including them behind your own login check.

## Usage

`FroalaField` stores the content in a text column and shows the editor in forms and the admin.

```python
from django.db import models
from froala_editor.fields import FroalaField

class Page(models.Model):
    content = FroalaField()
```

The field's widget, `froala_editor.widgets.FroalaEditor`, works in any form on its own.

```python
from django import forms
from froala_editor.widgets import FroalaEditor

class PageForm(forms.ModelForm):
    content = forms.CharField(widget=FroalaEditor)
```

### Outside the Admin

Outside the admin, include the form's media in the template, in the `<head>` or before the form. It loads the editor's scripts and styles, the plugins and the theme.

```html
{{ form.media }}
```

## Settings

A setting in `settings.py` applies to every editor in the project. The same name, as an argument to `FroalaField` or `FroalaEditor`, overrides it for one field.

| Setting | Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FROALA_EDITOR_OPTIONS` | `options` | The editor's [options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/), as a dictionary. An argument's options are merged over the setting's. |
| `FROALA_EDITOR_THEME` | `theme` | A theme, `'dark'`, `'gray'` or `'royal'`. |
| `FROALA_EDITOR_PLUGINS` | `plugins` | The plugins to load, as a tuple of file names. |
| `FROALA_EDITOR_THIRD_PARTY` | `third_party`, on the widget only | The third-party plugins to load, none by default. |
| `SCAYT_CUSTOMER_ID` |  | Your WebSpellChecker key, passed to the editor as `scaytCustomerId`. |

### Options

Your license key goes in the options, with any other option. A `language` in the setting also loads that language's file.

```python
# settings.py
FROALA_EDITOR_OPTIONS = {
    'key': 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY',
    'language': 'de',
}
```

```python
class Page(models.Model):
    content = FroalaField(options={'toolbarInline': True})

class PageForm(forms.ModelForm):
    content = forms.CharField(widget=FroalaEditor(options={'toolbarInline': True}))
```

### Theme

The package ships the dark, gray and royal themes, from `froala_editor/static/froala_editor/css/themes/`.

```python
content = FroalaField(theme='dark')
```

### Plugins

By default the package loads these [plugins](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/), with their stylesheets.

```python
FROALA_EDITOR_PLUGINS = (
    'align', 'char_counter', 'code_beautifier', 'code_view', 'colors', 'draggable', 'emoticons', 'entities', 'file',
    'font_family', 'font_size', 'fullscreen', 'help', 'image', 'image_manager', 'inline_style', 'line_breaker', 'link',
    'lists', 'paragraph_format', 'paragraph_style', 'print', 'quick_insert', 'quote', 'save', 'special_characters',
    'table', 'url', 'video', 'word_paste'
)
```

```python
content = FroalaField(plugins=('font_size', 'font_family'))
```

### Third-Party Plugins

The package ships `embedly`, `font_awesome`, `image_tui`, `imageFileRobot`, `showdown`, `spell_checker` and `yjs`. List the ones you want.

```python
# settings.py
FROALA_EDITOR_THIRD_PARTY = ('spell_checker',)
SCAYT_CUSTOMER_ID = 'YOUR_WEBSPELLCHECKER_ID'
```

### Uploads

The image view takes JPEG, PNG and GIF files. Files go to `FROALA_UPLOAD_PATH` in your storage, by default `uploads/froala_editor/images/` for images and `uploads/froala_editor/files/` for other files. Setting it puts both in the same folder.

The `image_upload` and `file_upload` arguments are accepted but change nothing. To turn uploads off for one field, set `imageUpload` or `fileUpload` to `False` in its options.

```python
content = FroalaField(options={'imageUpload': False, 'fileUpload': False})
```

### Other Settings

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `USE_FROALA_EDITOR` | `True` | When `False`, `FroalaField` shows a plain textarea. |
| `FROALA_STORAGE_BACKEND` | Django's default storage | The [storage class](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/stable/ref/files/storage/) for uploads, as a dotted path, such as an S3 backend for the editor only. |
| `FROALA_JS_COOKIE` | `False` | When `True`, the CSRF token is read with [js-cookie](https://github.com/js-cookie/js-cookie), which your page must load. |

## Additional Resources

- [Froala in a Django app with image upload](https://froala.com/blog/general/integrate-froala-to-django-web-application-with-image-upload/)
- [The best Django WYSIWYG editor with image upload](https://froala.com/blog/editor/whats-the-best-django-wysiwyg-editor-with-image-upload/)
- [Six server-side frameworks with WYSIWYG editor integration](https://froala.com/blog/general/6-server-side-frameworks-with-wysiwyg-editor-integration/)

# Ruby on Rails

The `wysiwyg-rails` gem serves the editor's scripts and stylesheets through the Rails asset pipeline, for Rails 3.2.7 up to Rails 8. Its source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-rails).

## Installation

Add the gem to your `Gemfile`, then run `bundle install`.

```ruby
gem "wysiwyg-rails"
```

```shell
bundle install
```

Each release of the gem bundles the editor of the same version, so updating the gem updates the editor.

The gem adds its files to Sprockets' `config.assets.precompile`. A Rails 8 app uses Propshaft by default, which has no such list, so add `sprockets-rails` to use the gem there.

## Include in Assets

Require the editor's stylesheets in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css`, with the stylesheets of the plugins you use and a theme if you want one.

```css
/*
 *= require froala_editor.min
 *= require froala_style.min
 *= require plugins/table.min
 *= require plugins/image.min
 *= require themes/dark.min
 */
```

In a Sass file such as `application.scss`, write `@import "froala_editor.min";` on its own line instead, not inside a comment.

Require the editor in `app/assets/javascripts/application.js`, then the plugins, a language and any third-party plugins.

```js
//= require froala_editor.min.js
//= require plugins/align.min.js
//= require plugins/image.min.js
//= require plugins/table.min.js
//= require languages/de.js
//= require third_party/embedly.min.js
```

Each plugin is `plugins/` and its file name, as in the [plugin list](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/). Only some plugins have a stylesheet. The gem also ships `froala_editor.pkgd.min.js` and `plugins.pkgd.min.js`, with every plugin in one file.

Restart the server after changing the requires.

## Initialize the Editor

Start the editor on an element in a view, with your license key and any other [options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/).

```erb
<%= form_with model: @post do |form| %>
  <%= form.text_area :body, id: "editor" %>
  <%= form.submit %>
<% end %>

<script>
  new FroalaEditor('#editor', {
    key: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY',
    language: 'de'
  });
</script>
```

On a textarea inside a form, the editor's content is sent with the form.

- [Installation](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/)
- [Ruby SDK, for image and file uploads](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/ruby/)

# Symfony `kms/froala-editor-bundle` adds a Froala form type, upload routes and a Twig display function to Symfony. Its source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/froala/KMSFroalaEditorBundle). ## Compatibility The bundle's latest release, from June 2024, requires Symfony 4.4 or 5 and PHP 7.2 or later. Symfony 6 and 7 are outside its requirements, so Composer won't install it there. On Symfony 6 or 7, load `froala-editor` with Webpack Encore or a CDN and start it on your form's textarea, as the [Installation guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/) shows. The [Webpack Encore](#webpack-encore) code below works without the bundle. ## Installation ### Install the Bundle ```shell composer require kms/froala-editor-bundle ``` With Symfony Flex and its recipe accepted, the next three steps are done for you. ### Register the Bundle ```php // config/bundles.php return [ // ... KMS\FroalaEditorBundle\KMSFroalaEditorBundle::class => ['all' => true], ]; ``` ### Import the Routes ```yaml # config/routes.yaml kms_froala_editor: resource: '@KMSFroalaEditorBundle/Resources/config/routing.yml' prefix: /froalaeditor ``` ### Load the Form Theme ```yaml # config/packages/twig.yaml twig: form_themes: - '@KMSFroalaEditor/Form/froala_widget.html.twig' ``` ### Configure the Bundle A language is required. Every other editor [option](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/) works here too. Give a list as an array and an object as a key and value array. Leave an option out to keep the editor's default. ```yaml # config/packages/kms_froala_editor.yaml kms_froala_editor: language: 'nl' serialNumber: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY' toolbarInline: true tableColors: ['#FFFFFF', '#FF0000'] saveParams: { 'id': 'myEditorField' } ``` These options belong to the bundle. | Option | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `serialNumber` | none | Your license key, passed to the editor as `key`. | | `includeFontAwesome` | `true` | Loads Font Awesome from a public CDN. Set it to `false` if you don't use it. | | `includeCodeMirror` | `true` | Loads CodeMirror from a public CDN, for the code view. | | `includeJS` | `true` | Loads the editor's scripts. Turn it off when your build loads them. | | `includeCSS` | `true` | Loads the editor's stylesheets. Turn it off when your build loads them. | | `basePath` | `/bundles/kmsfroalaeditor/froala_editor` | Where the editor's files are served from. | | `customJS` | none | A script of your own, for custom plugins and buttons. | ### Add the Editor to a Form Use the bundle's form type. Any option can be set per field, with the `froala_` prefix. ```php use KMS\FroalaEditorBundle\Form\Type\FroalaEditorType; $builder->add('content', FroalaEditorType::class, [ 'froala_language' => 'fr', 'froala_toolbarInline' => true, 'froala_tableColors' => ['#FFFFFF', '#FF0000'], 'froala_saveParams' => ['id' => 'myEditorField'], ]); ``` ### Install the Editor Files `froala:install` downloads the editor from its GitHub repository, the `master` branch unless you pass `--tag`, into the bundle's public folder. Then link the assets. ```shell bin/console froala:install bin/console assets:install --symlink public ``` The command takes a target folder as its argument, `--tag` for a given editor version, and `--clear` to replace a previous install. ### Display the Content `froala_display` prints saved content with the editor's styles. Without `includeCSS`, it leaves the stylesheet out. ```twig {{ froala_display(post.content) }} ``` Or include `froala_style.min.css` yourself and put the content in an element with the `fr-view` class. ```twig
{{ post.content|raw }}
``` Both print the HTML as it is. Clean content from users you don't trust before you show it. ## More Configuration ### Profiles A profile is a named set of options over the root ones, for forms that need them. ```yaml kms_froala_editor: heightMax: 400 profiles: tall: heightMax: 800 ``` ```php $builder->add('content', FroalaEditorType::class, ['froala_profile' => 'tall']); ``` ### Plugins Every [plugin](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/) is on by default. Turn some off, or list the only ones you want. A form field takes the same lists. ```yaml kms_froala_editor: pluginsDisabled: ['save', 'fullscreen'] # or pluginsEnabled: ['image', 'file'] ``` ### Image and File Upload The bundle's routes store [images](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/image/upload/), [files](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/file/upload/) and videos on your server, and list images for the image manager. | Option | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `imageUploadFolder` | `/upload` | The folder for images, inside your public folder. | | `imageUploadPath` | The folder | The URL base for images, when your assets use URL rewriting. | | `fileUploadFolder` | `/upload` | The folder for files, inside your public folder. | | `fileUploadPath` | The folder | The URL base for files. | | `publicDir` | `/public` | Your public folder, from the project root. | The upload, delete and image list routes don't check who is calling them. On a public site, protect the `/froalaeditor` prefix, for example with an `access_control` rule. ### Autosave The editor's [autosave](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/save/autosave/) options work as they are. `saveURLParams`, from the bundle, adds parameters to build the save route. ```yaml kms_froala_editor: saveURL: 'my_save_route' saveURLParams: { 'id': 'myId' } saveInterval: 2500 saveParam: 'content' ``` ### Webpack Encore To load the editor from npm with Webpack Encore, import it in your entry, then turn off the bundle's own files. ```js import FroalaEditor from 'froala-editor'; import 'froala-editor/css/froala_editor.pkgd.min.css'; import 'froala-editor/css/froala_style.min.css'; import 'froala-editor/js/plugins.pkgd.min.js'; import 'froala-editor/css/plugins.pkgd.min.css'; import 'froala-editor/js/languages/fr.js'; window.FroalaEditor = FroalaEditor; ``` ```yaml kms_froala_editor: includeJS: false includeCSS: false ``` ## Additional Resources - [The bundle's README](https://github.com/froala/KMSFroalaEditorBundle#readme) - [PHP SDK](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/php/) - [A support system with Laravel and Froala, part 1](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/building-a-support-system-using-laravel-php-framework-and-froala-rich-text-editor-part-1/) - [Froala image management in Laravel](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/simplify-froala-image-management-in-laravel-using-froala-html-code-writer/) - [A support system with Laravel and Froala, part 3](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/building-laravel-support-system-part-3-froala-html-editor-software/)
