Froala Editor. ``` ``` Froala Editor can initialize on more elements than other editors: - Froala can be initiated on an image using the image.min.js plugin ``` ``` - It is possible to initialize the Froala Editor only on a button ``` ``` - It is possible to initialize the Froala Editor on click on an element ```
Hello ContentTools
``` ### 2\. Working with plugins Trix does not use plugins. Froala Editor has over 30 plugins, you can specify required plugins at initialization. **Note:** By default, all plugins are enabled without using the pluginsEnabled option. Also, each plugin requires you to include the corresponding JS and CSS files. Here is the [complete list of plugins](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/) and the files required by them. Froala Editor ``` new FroalaEditor('#editor', { pluginsEnabled: ['image', 'link'] }); ``` If you do not find the plugin you want, you can create your own. ### 3\. ### aiAssistDataKeys

Type:

Object | null

Default:

```
null
```

Plugin:

ai\_assist.min.js

Custom mapping for request data keys. Use this to match your API's expected field names.  
  
**Available Keys:**

-   `id`: Field name for ID (default: `'id'`)
-   `idValue`: Value for ID field (default: `""`)
-   `question`: Field name for question/prompt (default: `'question'`)
-   `questionOrderNumber`: Field name for question order (default: `'question_order_number'`)
-   `questionOrderNumberValue`: Value for question order (default: `1`)
-   `sessionId`: Field name for session ID (default: `'session_id'`)
-   `sessionIdValue`: Value for session ID (default: `"new_session"`)
-   `timestamp`: Field name for timestamp (default: `'question_timestamp'`)

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  aiAssistDataKeys: {
    question: 'prompt',
    sessionId: 'conversation_id',
    sessionIdValue: 'user-123-session',
    questionOrderNumber: 'message_index',
  }
});
```

### aiAssistRequest

Type:

Function | null

Default:

```
null
```

Plugin:

ai\_assist.min.js

Custom function to handle AI requests. If provided, this overrides the default endpoint-based approach (aiAssistEndpoint), letting you call any AI provider, Groq, Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, or your own backend, directly from the browser or through your own server.

#### FUNCTION SIGNATURE

```
async function(data, signal, onChunk) => string | { answer: string, session_id?: string, webSearchUsed?: boolean }
```

#### PARAMETERS

**data** (object): Everything Froala knows about the request. Always includes `prompt`, `context`, `question`, `session_id`, and `question_order_number`, it may also include:

`webSearchEnabled`

Boolean - present only if the web-search toggle was on when the message was sent.

`model`

String - the `modelName` the user picked from `aiChatModels`, present only if that option is configured.

`reasoningEnabled`

Boolean - present only if the reasoning toggle was on.

`files`

Array - attached files, already read and encoded client-side. PDFs/images arrive as `{ name, mimeType, base64 }`; TXT/MD/DOCX arrive as `{ name, mimeType, textContent }` (DOCX text is Mammoth-converted HTML).

`referenceUrls`

Array of strings - plain URLs added as "Reference URL" context sources.

`regenerate`

Boolean - present only when the user clicks Try again on an AI Assist response. If your backend caches or deduplicates identical prompts, use it to return a fresh answer.

**signal** (AbortSignal): Pass this straight into your `fetch` call so the request can be cancelled if the user navigates away or cancels mid-request.

**onChunk** (function, optional): If AI Chat is requesting a streamed answer, Froala calls your handler with this as a third argument. Call `onChunk(text)` yourself each time a new piece of the answer arrives from your provider. If you don't declare or use this parameter, Froala simply waits for your function to resolve the full answer instead, exactly as it did before this version.

#### RETURNS

A `Promise` that resolves to either of two shapes:

**1\. A plain string** The string is treated as the answer text, and no web-search badge is shown (equivalent to resolving `webSearchUsed: false`).

**2\. An object** — `{ answer: string, session_id?: string, webSearchUsed?: boolean }`. Resolve this shape instead of a plain string when you want to report back whether your AI provider actually performed a web search, `webSearchUsed` is then surfaced through `aiChatAssistant.getChatHistory()` and shown as a badge on the response. Turning the web-search toggle on only asks the model to search if it decides to; it doesn't guarantee a search happened, so this field is the only way Froala knows for sure. `session_id` is used internally for session continuity. This return contract is the same whether or not `onChunk` was used - a streaming handler resolves this only after it has finished calling `onChunk` with every chunk, exactly as a non-streaming handler resolves it immediately.

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  aiAssistRequest: async function (data, signal, onChunk) {
    // data.webSearchEnabled / data.model / data.reasoningEnabled / data.files /
    // data.referenceUrls are present only when the corresponding toggle or
    // context source was actually used.

    const response = await fetch(
      'https://my-ai-api.com/generate',
      {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({
          prompt: data.prompt,
          webSearchEnabled: data.webSearchEnabled,
          context: data.context,
          noCache: data.regenerate === true
        }),
        signal
      }
    );

    if (onChunk) {
      // Handle a streaming response from your provider here,
      // calling onChunk(chunkText) as each piece arrives.
    }

    const result = await response.json();

    // Resolving an object (instead of a plain string) lets you report
    // back whether your provider actually used web search.
    return {
      answer: result.answer,
      webSearchUsed: !!result.usedWebSearch,
      session_id: result.session_id
    };
  }
});
```

### collabConfig.commentsUrl

Type:

String | null

Default:

```
null
```

Plugin:

collaborative.min.js

Base URL for the comments REST API. Used in **both real-time and asynchronous collaboration** to persist comment data to the database and retrieve it back. In real-time mode, comment data is saved to the database through this URL and fetched back on initialization; in asynchronous mode, it is the primary source for fetching and managing all comment data.

-   `GET` requests retrieve the list of comments
-   `POST` requests create new comments
-   `PATCH / DELETE` requests target a specific comment by automatically appending `/{id}` to the URL

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  collabConfig: {
    user: {
      id: 'user-id',
      name: 'user-name',
      role: 'suggester',
    },
    docId: 'my-doc',
    commentsUrl: 'http://localhost:3000/collab/my-doc/comments'
  }
});
```

A unique identifier for the document. This is required for **both real-time and asynchronous collaboration** — it is used to associate all collaborative data (comments, suggestions, and version history) with the correct document. ### collabConfig.realTime.syncUrl

Type:

String | null

Default:

```
null
```

Plugin:

collaborative.min.js

WebSocket server URL used for real-time collaboration. This is the **main switch that enables real-time collab** across the entire plugin — when set, all collaborative features (live editing, comments, suggestions, and version control) are synchronized instantly between connected editors over this WebSocket connection.  
  
In real-time mode, comments, suggestions, and version control data are shared live between all users connected to the same `docId` for the duration of their session. This data is only available as long as at least one user remains connected — it is not persisted automatically. To persist this data to the database, the respective URLs (`commentsUrl, suggestionsUrl`, and `versionControl.url`) must be configured.  
  
If `null`, the plugin falls back to asynchronous (offline-first) mode, relying on `commentsUrl, suggestionsUrl`, and `versionControl.url` instead.

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  collabConfig: {
    user: {
      id: 'user-id',
      name: 'user-name',
      role: 'suggester',
    },
    docId: 'my-doc',
    commentsUrl: 'http://localhost:3000/collab/my-doc/comments',
    suggestionsUrl: 'http://localhost:3000/collab/my-doc/suggection',
    realTime: {
      syncUrl: 'ws://localhost:3000'
    }
  }
});
```

### collabConfig.versionControl.url

Type:

string | null

Default:

```
null
```

Plugin:

collaborative.min.js

Base URL for the version history REST API. Used in **both real-time and asynchronous collaboration** to persist version snapshot data to the database and retrieve it back. In real-time mode, version snapshot data is saved to the database through this URL and fetched back on initialization; in asynchronous mode, it is the primary source for fetching and managing all version snapshot data.

-   `GET` requests retrieve the list of snapshots
-   `POST` requests create new snapshots
-   `PATCH / DELETE` requests target a specific snapshot by automatically appending `/{id}` to the URL

If you want to enable version control **without persisting to the database**, set `versionControl` to an empty object `{}`. In this mode, version snapshots are stored locally in memory only — they remain available until the page is reloaded, at which point they are cleared. In real-time mode, locally saved versions are still shared with other editors connected to the same `docId` via WebSocket for the duration of the session, but are lost once the session ends.

new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  collabConfig: {
    user: {
      id: 'user-id',
      name: 'user-name',
      role: 'suggester',
    },
    docId: 'my-doc',
    versionControl: {
      url: 'http://localhost:3000/collab/my-doc/versions'
    }
  }
});
```

Set the options for image upload to S3. All the fields from the example below are required. Also make sure that you have enabled [CORS](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/cors.html "CORS") on Amazon.  
  
**Note:** `uploadURL` property can be used instead of `bucket` and `region` properties to specify a custom URL from Amazon where to upload the image.

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  imageUploadToS3: {
    bucket: 'editor',
    // Your bucket region.
    region: 's3-us-east-1',
    keyStart: 'uploads/',
    params: {
      acl: 'public-read', // ACL according to Amazon Documentation.
      AWSAccessKeyId: 'ACCESS_KEY', // Access Key from Amazon.
      policy: 'POLICY_STRING', // Policy string computed in the backend.
      signature: '', // Signature computed in the backend.

      // If you are using Amazon Signature V4, the followings should be used instead.
      // "X-Amz-Credential": "...",
      // "X-Amz-Algorithm": "AWS4-HMAC-SHA256",
      // "X-Amz-Date": "...",
      // Policy: "...", //
      // "X-Amz-Signature": "", // computed in backend
    }
  }
});
```

### imageUploadURL

Type:

String

Default:

```
null
```

Plugin:

image.min.js

The URL where the images uploaded by the user are saved. When an image is uploaded, the editor sends the file to the server through a HTTP request. The server should process the data from the `file` parameter of the request and return a JSON object containing a `link` field with the link to the uploaded image. More details can be found in the [Image Upload](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/image/upload/ "Image Upload Concept") concept article.  
**E.g.** {link: 'path/to/image.jpg'}.  
  
**Note 1:** By default, the images are stored on our servers, but if you want to have full control over them, you should consider implementing the upload on your server. The images stored on our servers, may be deleted at any time without any notice.  
**Note 2:** If the domain where the image is saved is not the same with the one where the editor is running, you may need to enable [requestWithCORS](#requestWithCORS "requestWithCORS") option and make specific customizations on the server. For more information please refer to [Cross-origin resource sharing](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-origin_resource_sharing "Cross-origin Resource Sharing").

#### CODE EXAMPLE

new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  imageUploadURL: 'http://i.froala.com/upload'
});

Type:

Plugin:

Core (no plugin file)

Runs the editor with no built-in toolbar, popups, or other UI, so you can build your own controls and drive everything through the editor’s API instead. This is read once when the editor is created — changing it afterward has no effect, so you’d need to create a new editor instance to turn it on or off.

});

### imageManagerLoadURL

Type:

```

Plugin:

image\_manager.min.js

The URL where the HTTP request is done in order to load a page of images that appear in the image manager. The response should be an array with an Object for each image, similar to:

```
[
  {
    url: 'http://exmaple.com/images/photo1.jpg',
    thumb: "http://exmaple.com/thumbs/photo1.jpg",
    tag: 'flower'
  },
  {
    url: 'http://exmaple.com/images/photo2.jpg',
    thumb: "http://exmaple.com/thumbs/photo2.jpg",
    tag: 'sport'
  }
]
```

  
Where `url` is required, `thumb` is recommended and `tag` is optional. The image Object may also contain additional data that will be saved as image attributes `data-*`. E.g.:

```
[
  {
    url: 'http://exmaple.com/images/photo1.jpg',
    thumb: "http://exmaple.com/thumbs/photo1.jpg",
    tag: 'flower',
    name: "Photo 1 Name",
    id: 103454285,
  }
]
```

`<img src='https://exmaple.com/images/photo1.jpg' data-name='Photo 1 Name' data-id='103454285'>`

### videoUploadToS3

Type:

Object

Default:

```

```

Plugin:

video.min.js

Set the options for video upload to S3. All the fields from the example below are required. Also make sure that you have enabled [CORS](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/cors.html "CORS") on Amazon.  
  
**Note:** `uploadURL` property can be used instead of `bucket` and `region` properties to specify a custom URL from Amazon where to upload the video.

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  videoUploadToS3: {
    bucket: 'editor',
    // Your bucket region.
    region: 's3-us-east-1',
    keyStart: 'uploads/',
    params: {
      acl: 'public-read', // ACL according to Amazon Documentation.
      AWSAccessKeyId: 'ACCESS_KEY', // Access Key from Amazon.
      policy: 'POLICY_STRING', // Policy string computed in the backend.
      signature: '', // Signature computed in the backend.

      // If you are using Amazon Signature V4, the followings should be used instead.
      // "X-Amz-Credential": "...",
      // "X-Amz-Algorithm": "AWS4-HMAC-SHA256",
      // "X-Amz-Date": "...",
      // Policy: "...", //
      // "X-Amz-Signature": "", // computed in backend
    }
  }
});
```

### videoUploadURL

Type:

String

Default:

```
null
```

Plugin:

video.min.js

The URL where the videos uploaded by the user are saved. When a video is uploaded, the editor sends the file to the server through a HTTP request. The server should process the data from the `file` parameter of the request and return a JSON object containing a `link` field with the link to the uploaded video.  
  
**Note 1:** By default, the videos are stored on our servers, but if you want to have full control over them, you should consider implementing the upload on your server. The videos stored on our servers, may be deleted at any time without any notice.  
**Note 2:** If the domain where the video is saved is not the same with the one where the editor is running, you may need to enable [requestWithCORS](#requestWithCORS "requestWithCORS") option and make specific customizations on the server. For more information please refer to [Cross-origin resource sharing](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-origin_resource_sharing "Cross-origin Resource Sharing").

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  videoUploadURL: '/upload_video'
});
```

## Files Manager

[filesManagerAllowedTypes](#filesManagerAllowedTypes "filesManagerAllowedTypes") [filesManagerMaxSize](#filesManagerMaxSize "filesManagerMaxSize") [filesManagerUploadParams](#filesManagerUploadParams "filesManagerUploadParams") [filesManagerUploadToS3](#filesManagerUploadToS3 "filesManagerUploadToS3") [filesManagerUploadURL](#filesManagerUploadURL "filesManagerUploadURL")

### filesManagerAllowedTypes

Type:

Array

Default:

```
['*']
```

Plugin:

files\_manager.min.js

The list of file types that are allowed to be uploaded. Although this will restrict uploading other types of files, we strongly recommend you to check the file type on the server too.

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  filesManagerAllowedTypes: [
    'application/pdf', 
    'application/msword',
    ‘video/mp4’, 
    ‘video/webm’, 
    ‘image/png’
  ]

```

### filesManagerMaxSize

Type:

Number

Default:

```
1024 * 1024 *10
```

Plugin:

files\_manager.min.js

The maximum file size allowed on upload in bytes. The default value is 10MB. Although this makes an additional check before uploading the file, it is highly recommended to check file size on your server too.

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```

### filesManagerUploadParams

Type:

Object

Default:

```
{}
```

Plugin:

files\_manager.min.js

Pass additional parameters to the file upload request.

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```

  filesManagerUploadParams: {
    id: 'my_editor'
  }
});
```

### filesManagerUploadToS3

Type:

Object

Default:

```
false
```

Plugin:

files\_manager.min.js

Set the options for file upload to S3. All the fields from the example below are required. Also make sure that you have enabled [CORS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/cors.html) on Amazon.  
**Note:** `uploadURL` property can be used instead of `bucket` and `region` properties to specify a custom URL from Amazon where to upload the image.

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  filesManagerUploadToS3: {
    bucket: 'editor',
    region: 's3',
    keyStart: 'uploads/',
    params:{ 
       acl: 'public-read', // ACL according to Amazon Documentation.
       AWSAccessKeyId: 'ACCESS_KEY', // Access Key from Amazon. 
       policy: 'POLICY_STRING', // Policy string computed in the backend.
       signature: '', // Signature computed in the backend.
        // If you are using Amazon Signature V4, the followings should beused instead.
        // "X-Amz-Credential": "...",
        // "X-Amz-Algorithm": "AWS4-HMAC-SHA256",
        // "X-Amz-Date": "...",
        // Policy: "...", //
        // "X-Amz-Signature": "", // computed in backend
       }
   }
});
```

### filesManagerUploadURL

Type:

String

Default:

```
http://i.froala.com/upload
```

Plugin:

files\_manager.min.js

The URL where the files uploaded by the user are saved. When a file is uploaded, the editor sends the file to the server through a HTTP request. The server should process the data from the `file` parameter of the request and return a JSON object containing a link field with the `link` to the uploaded file.  
`**E.g.** {link: 'path/to/file.pdf'}`  
  
**Note 1:** By default, the files are stored on our servers, but if you want to have full control over them, you should consider implementing the upload on your server. The files stored on our servers, may be deleted at any time without any notice.  
**Note 2:** If the domain where the file is saved is not the same with the one where the editor is running, you may need to enable [requestWithCORS](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#requestWithCORS) option and make specific customizations on the server. For more information please refer to [Cross-origin resource sharing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-origin_resource_sharing).

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  filesManagerUploadURL: '/upload_file'
});
```

#### CODE EXAMPLE

```

```

# Installation Install with npm or a CDN, then start the editor in your framework. ## 1. Install the Package Install the latest Froala from npm, with its wrapper for React, Vue or Angular, or see the [other supported technologies](#other-supported-technologies). **React** ```shell npm install froala-editor react-froala-wysiwyg ``` **TypeScript** ```shell npm install froala-editor ``` **Vue** ```shell npm install froala-editor vue-froala-wysiwyg ``` **Angular** ```shell npm install froala-editor angular-froala-wysiwyg ``` **JavaScript** ```shell npm install froala-editor ``` ## 2. Start an Editor **React** ```jsx import 'froala-editor/css/froala_style.min.css'; import 'froala-editor/css/froala_editor.pkgd.min.css'; import 'froala-editor/js/plugins.pkgd.min.js'; import FroalaEditorComponent from 'react-froala-wysiwyg'; const config = { // key: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY', placeholderText: 'Start writing', }; export default function App() { return ; } ``` [React guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/react/) **TypeScript** ```ts import FroalaEditor, { type FroalaOptions } from 'froala-editor'; import 'froala-editor/css/froala_editor.pkgd.min.css'; import 'froala-editor/js/plugins.pkgd.min.js'; const config: Partial = { // key: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY', placeholderText: 'Start writing', }; const host = document.querySelector('#editor')!; const editor = new FroalaEditor(host, config); ``` [All options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/) **Vue** ```vue // main.js import VueFroala from 'vue-froala-wysiwyg'; import 'froala-editor/css/froala_editor.pkgd.min.css'; import 'froala-editor/js/plugins.pkgd.min.js'; app.use(VueFroala); // App.vue ``` [Vue guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/vue-js-3/) **Angular** ```ts // styles.css @import 'froala-editor/css/froala_editor.pkgd.min.css'; import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { FroalaEditorModule, FroalaViewModule } from 'angular-froala-wysiwyg'; import 'froala-editor/js/plugins.pkgd.min.js'; @Component({ selector: 'app-editor', standalone: true, imports: [FroalaEditorModule, FroalaViewModule], template: '
' }) export class EditorComponent { options = { placeholderText: 'Start writing' }; // key: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY' model = '

Hello from Froala

Start writing here.

'; } ``` [Angular guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/angular/) **JavaScript** ```html

Hello from Froala

Start writing here.

``` [CDN guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/install-froala-cdn/) For a simpler editor, give the config a toolbar of your own. Small screens have toolbar lists of their own, so set those too. The result below runs this one. ```js const simple = [ ['undo', 'redo'], ['paragraphFormat'], ['bold', 'italic', 'underline'], ['insertLink', 'insertImage'], ['formatUL', 'formatOL'] ]; const config = { placeholderText: 'Start writing', toolbarButtons: simple, toolbarButtonsSM: simple, toolbarButtonsXS: simple }; ``` ## 3. Add Your License Key Pass it as `key` in the editor's options, in any stack above. ```js new FroalaEditor('#editor', { key: 'YOUR_LICENSE_KEY' }); ``` No key yet? [Start a free trial](https://froala.com/wysiwyg_editor-download/) with every feature for 30 days, or read the [activation guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/activation/). ## Load from a CDN For pages without a build step. ```html
``` Pin a version in place of `@latest` for production. ## Other Ways to Install - [Download a starter project](https://froala.com/wysiwyg_editor-download/) - [Using AMD](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/install-froala-amd/) - [Using Bower](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/install-froala-bower/) - [Using CommonJS](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/install-froala-commonjs/) - [Using UMD](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/install-froala-umd/) ## Other Supported Technologies Guides for 15 more frameworks and CMSs, and SDKs for 6 server languages. ### Front-end Frameworks - [Svelte (npm)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/svelte/) - [Gatsby (npm)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/gatsby/) - [Ember (ember install)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/ember/) - [Ionic (Guide)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/ionic/) - [Sencha Ext JS (Open Tools)](https://docs.sencha.com/extjs/7.4.0/guides/components/froala.html) ### Back-end Frameworks and CMSs - [Django (pip)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/django/) - [Ruby on Rails (gem)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/rails/) - [Symfony (Composer)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/symfony/) - [CakePHP (git clone)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/cakephp/) - [Yii (npm)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/yii/) - [Craft CMS (Composer)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/craft-cms/) - [Node.js](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/nodejs/) - [PHP](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/php/) - [Python](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/python/) - [Ruby](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/ruby/) ## Next Steps - # Install with Bower ## Step 1. Install From [Bower](https://libraries.io/bower/froala-wysiwyg-editor) Run the following command. ```shell bower install froala-wysiwyg-editor ``` After the installation process is finished, add this code to your HTML file. ```html ``` ## Step 2. Create DOM Element The Froala Editor is quite flexible and can be initialized to ‘attach’ to any standard HTML DOM element, such as a DIV, or a TEXTAREA. pages.title: Plugins
pages.markdown:
# Plugins

Everything beyond the core editor is a plugin. Load them all in one file, or only the ones you use.

Every plugin works with any key.

## Load Plugins

### Every Plugin

`froala_editor.pkgd.min.js` holds the editor and every plugin in `js/plugins` except Track Changes and Trim Video, and `plugins.pkgd.min.js` holds the same plugins without the editor. Third-party plugins are in neither.

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/froala_editor.pkgd.min.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/froala_editor.pkgd.min.js"></script>
```

With npm, import the plugins after the editor.

```js
import FroalaEditor from 'froala-editor';
import 'froala-editor/css/froala_editor.pkgd.min.css';
import 'froala-editor/js/plugins.pkgd.min.js';
```

### Some Plugins

Load the core editor, then each plugin's script and, if it has one, its stylesheet. The Table plugin, for example, takes these.

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/froala_editor.min.css" rel="stylesheet">
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/plugins/table.min.css" rel="stylesheet">

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/froala_editor.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/table.min.js"></script>
```

```js
import FroalaEditor from 'froala-editor';
import 'froala-editor/css/froala_editor.min.css';
import 'froala-editor/css/plugins/table.min.css';
import 'froala-editor/js/plugins/table.min.js';
```

### Turn Plugins On and Off

Every loaded plugin is on by default. `pluginsEnabled` keeps only the plugins it names, and `pluginsDisabled` turns off the ones it names. Both take the names in the table below. A plugin in both lists stays off.

```js
new FroalaEditor('#editor', {
  pluginsEnabled: ['table', 'image', 'link']
});
```

## Available Plugins

The files are `js/plugins/<file>.min.js` and, where the table says CSS, `css/plugins/<file>.min.css`. The name is the one `pluginsEnabled` takes.

| Plugin | What it does | Name | Files |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [AI Assist](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/ai-assist-plugin/) | AI writing and editing tools, with a chat panel, reviewable edits, dictation and autocomplete, through the AI provider you connect. Needs `aiSupplementalTermsAccepted: true`. | `aiAssist` | `ai_assist` JS and CSS |
| [Align](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/align-plugin/) | Aligns paragraphs left, center, right or justified. | `align` | `align` JS |
| [Anchor](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/link-to-anchor-plugin/) | Adds named anchors and links to them. | `linkToAnchor` | `link_to_anchor` JS and CSS |
| [Char Counter](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/char-counter-plugin/) | Counts characters in the bottom bar, and can cap them with `charCounterMax`. | `charCounter` | `char_counter` JS and CSS |
| [Code Beautifier](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/code-beautifier-plugin/) | Formats the HTML in code view. | `codeBeautifier` | `code_beautifier` JS |
| [Code Snippet](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/code-snippet-plugin/) | Inserts code blocks with syntax highlighting. Needs Prism.js on the page. | `codeSnippet` | `code_snippet` JS and CSS |
| [Code View](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/code-view-plugin/) | Shows and edits the content's HTML. | `codeView` | `code_view` JS and CSS |
| [Collaborative](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/collaborative-plugin/) | Real-time editing, comments, suggestions and version history. | `collaborative` | `collaborative` JS and CSS |
| [Colors](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/colors-plugin/) | Changes the text and background colors. | `colors` | `colors` JS and CSS |
| [Draggable](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/draggable-plugin/) | Drags images and videos to a new place in the content. | `draggable` | `draggable` JS and CSS |
| [Edit in Popup](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/examples/edit-in-popup/) | Edits the text of the element the editor runs on in a popup, instead of in place. A module, not a plugin, so it has no plugin name; turn it on with `editInPopup: true`. | None | `edit_in_popup` JS |
| [Emoticons](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/emoticons-plugin/) | Inserts emoticons from a picker. | `emoticons` | `emoticons` JS and CSS |
| [Entities](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/entities-plugin/) | Converts special characters to HTML entities, such as © to `©`. | `entities` | `entities` JS |
| [Export to Word](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/export-to-word-plugin/) | Exports the content to a Word (.docx) file. Needs the html-docx-js and FileSaver libraries. | `exportToWord` | `export_to_word` JS |
| [File](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/file-plugin/) | Uploads any type of file and inserts a link to download it. | `file` | `file` JS and CSS |
| [Files Manager](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/files-manager-plugin/) | Uploads files of any type, one or several at a time, and inserts, shows and deletes them. | `filesManager` | `files_manager` JS and CSS |
| [Filestack](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/filestack-plugin/) | Uploads files through Filestack, with its file and image transformations. Needs a Filestack API key. | `filestack` | `filestack` JS and CSS |
| [Find and Replace](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/find-replace-plugin/) | Finds text in the content and replaces it. | `findReplace` | `find_and_replace` JS and CSS |
| [Font Family](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/font-family-plugin/) | Sets the font of the selected text. | `fontFamily` | `font_family` JS |
| [Font Size](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/font-size-plugin/) | Sets the size of the selected text. | `fontSize` | `font_size` JS |
| [Forms](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#formEditButtons) | Edits the text and style of buttons, inputs and text areas in the content. | `forms` | `forms` JS |
| [Fullscreen](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/fullscreen-plugin/) | Opens the editor full screen. | `fullscreen` | `fullscreen` JS and CSS |
| [Help](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/help-plugin/) | Lists the keyboard shortcuts in a popup. | `help` | `help` JS and CSS |
| [Image](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/image-plugin/) | Inserts, uploads and edits images. | `image` | `image` JS and CSS |
| [Image Manager](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/image-manager-plugin/) | Browses and deletes images on your server. | `imageManager` | `image_manager` JS and CSS |
| [Import from Word](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/import-from-word-plugin/) | Imports a Word (.docx) file into the editor. Converts it in the browser with Mammoth.js, or on your server. | `importFromWord` | `import_from_word` JS |
| [Inline Class](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/inline-class-plugin/) | Applies classes you define to the selected text. | `inlineClass` | `inline_class` JS |
| [Inline Style](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/inline-style-plugin/) | Applies styles you define to the selected text. | `inlineStyle` | `inline_style` JS |
| [Line Breaker](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/line-breaker-plugin/) | Adds a new line between elements such as tables. | `lineBreaker` | `line_breaker` JS and CSS |
| [Line Height](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/line-height-plugin/) | Sets the line height of the selected paragraphs. | `lineHeight` | `line_height` JS |
| [Link](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/link-plugin/) | Inserts and edits links. | `link` | `link` JS |
| [Lists](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/lists-plugin/) | Inserts ordered and unordered lists. | `lists` | `lists` JS |
| [Markdown](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/markdown-plugin/) | Writes the content in Markdown syntax, with a split view of the result. | `markdown` | `markdown` JS and CSS |
| [Page Break](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/page-break-plugin/) | Inserts, moves and shows page breaks. | `pageBreak` | `page_break` JS and CSS |
| [Paragraph Format](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/paragraph-format-plugin/) | Changes a paragraph's type, such as a heading. | `paragraphFormat` | `paragraph_format` JS |
| [Paragraph Style](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/paragraph-style-plugin/) | Applies a style you define to a paragraph. | `paragraphStyle` | `paragraph_style` JS |
| Print | Adds Print and Download PDF buttons. The PDF needs the html2pdf.js library. | `print` | `print` JS |
| [Quick Insert](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/quick-insert-plugin/) | Shows a button on an empty line to insert images, videos, tables, lists and more. | `quickInsert` | `quick_insert` JS and CSS |
| [Quote](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/quote-plugin/) | Adds quotes with several levels. | `quote` | `quote` JS |
| [Save](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/save-plugin/) | Saves the content to your server with AJAX, on demand or as the user types. | `save` | `save` JS |
| [Special Characters](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/special-characters-plugin/) | Inserts special characters. | `specialCharacters` | `special_characters` JS and CSS |
| [Table](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/table-plugin/) | Inserts tables and edits their cells, rows and columns. | `table` | `table` JS and CSS |
| [Track Changes](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/track-changes-plugin/) | Tracks added and deleted content and formatting, so each change can be accepted or rejected. Not in `plugins.pkgd.min.js`. | `track_changes` | `track_changes` JS |
| Trim Video | Trims a video in the Files Manager before it is inserted, through a conversion server you run (it posts to `http://localhost:3000/convert`). Not in `plugins.pkgd.min.js`. | `trimVideoPlugin` | `trim_video` JS and CSS |
| [URL](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/url-plugin/) | Turns URLs into links as you type. | `url` | `url` JS |
| [Video](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/video-plugin/) | Inserts videos by URL or embed code. | `video` | `video` JS and CSS |
| [Word Counter](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/word-counter-plugin/) | Counts words in the bottom bar, and can cap them with `wordCounterMax`. | `wordCounter` | `word_counter` JS |
| [Word Paste](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/word-paste-plugin/) | Cleans the HTML pasted from Word. | `wordPaste` | `word_paste` JS |

## Third-Party Plugins

These connect the editor to another product. Their files are `js/third_party/<file>.min.js` and `css/third_party/<file>.min.css`, and no packaged file includes them.

| Plugin | What it does | Name | Files |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Embedly](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/embedly-plugin/) | Embeds content from the web. Loads Embedly's platform script from cdn.embedly.com. | `embedly` | `embedly` JS and CSS |
| [Font Awesome](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/font-awesome-plugin/) | Inserts Font Awesome icons. Needs the Font Awesome stylesheet. | `fontAwesome` | `font_awesome` JS and CSS |
| [Image Filerobot](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/filerobot-image-editor-plugin/) | Edits images in Filerobot Image Editor, with annotations, filters, resizing, rotation and watermarks. Needs the Filerobot library. | `imageFilerobot` | `imageFileRobot` JS and CSS |
| [Image TUI](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/image-tui-plugin/) | Edits images in TOAST UI Image Editor, with filters, frames, stickers and touch-up tools. Needs the TOAST UI Image Editor library. | `imageTUI` | `image_tui` JS and CSS |
| [Spell Checker](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/spell-checker-plugin/) | Shows and corrects misspellings as you type, through the WebSpellChecker service. | `spellChecker` | `spell_checker` JS and CSS |

## Helper Files

Three more files ship with the plugins. They add no feature of their own.

| File | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| `js/plugins/cryptojs.min.js` | The CryptoJS library. The Image, Video, File and Files Manager plugins use it to sign uploads to Azure. |
| `js/third_party/showdown.min.js` | The Showdown Markdown converter. The Markdown plugin file already includes it. |
| `js/third_party/yjs.min.js` | The Yjs library. The Collaborative plugin file already includes it. |

## Create a Plugin

A plugin is a function on `FroalaEditor.PLUGINS` that gets the editor instance and returns its public methods. The editor calls `_init` when each instance starts. A plugin that doesn't return it still offers its other methods; nothing of it runs at start. The [custom plugin guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/custom/plugin/) covers options and headless mode.

```js
FroalaEditor.PLUGINS.myPlugin = function (editor) {
  function _init() {
    // Runs when each editor starts.
  }

  function wordCount() {
    return editor.el.textContent.trim().split(/\s+/).length;
  }

  // Public methods, called as editor.myPlugin.wordCount().
  return { _init: _init, wordCount: wordCount };
};
```

## Additional Resources

- [The Modular Architecture of the Froala HTML Editor](https://froala.com/blog/general/building-more-robust-and-scalable-software-a-closer-at-froala-html-editor-software/)
- [How to Build a Custom Plugin](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/custom/plugin/)
- [Extend Froala with an APA Website Citation Tool](https://froala.com/blog/editor/extending-froala-with-an-apa-website-citation-tool/)

pages.title: AI Assist Plugin
pages.markdown:
# AI Assist Plugin

Give your users AI writing and editing tools directly inside the Froala editor, including a full chat panel, reviewable AI edits, dictation, and inline autocomplete.

**Froala is provider-agnostic.** We don't ship an AI model, and AI Assist sends no prompt or content to Froala. You plug in your own provider (OpenAI, Groq, Google Gemini, Anthropic, or your own backend) with one function, and your content goes straight from the browser to the provider you chose.

To use AI features in Froala, you need to accept the [AI Supplemental Terms](https://www.ideracorp.com/legal/Froala#tabs-2) by setting the `aiSupplementalTermsAccepted` option to true in your configuration.

## Features

The AI Assist plugin bundles six features. All of them share the same connection to your AI provider, so you set that up once.

### AI Chat Assistant

A collapsible, resizable chat panel docked to the right of the editor. Users hold a real back-and-forth conversation with the AI. They ask follow-up questions, summarise, brainstorm, then choose whether to put anything into the document.

- Streaming responses (the answer types itself out as it arrives).
- Context from the whole document, the current selection, uploaded files (PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD, images), or a reference URL.
- Web search and reasoning toggles, plus a model picker you supply. If the selected model does not support a toggle, it turns off automatically and a short notice explains why.
- “Apply to document” shows a diff of what will change before it commits.

### AI Image Generation

Users can describe their desired image in the AI Assist prompt, and your configured AI model returns image(s). Your backend sends each image as an `img` element in an HTML answer, which the popup shows as it will be inserted. Users then have three choices.

- Preview the generated image in the AI Assist popup before inserting.
- Insert the image at the current cursor position.
- Regenerate to request a new variant from the same prompt.

### AI Improve Writing

Select any text and a small floating button appears. Click it, and the AI’s rewrite comes back as tracked changes. Users step through changes one at a time, or use Accept All / Reject All.

### Speech-to-Text Prompting

A microphone button inside the AI prompt popup. Users dictate instead of typing; the recording goes to your AI backend with `speechToText` set, and the transcript it returns lands in the prompt box and stays editable before they send it.

### Inline Suggestions (Ghost Text)

Autocomplete in the style of Gmail Smart Compose. Pause at the end of a paragraph and a greyed-out continuation appears at the caret. Tab accepts it, Esc dismisses it, and just carrying on typing ignores it. Nothing enters the document until Tab is pressed.

### One-Click Tone and Translate

Select text and instantly change its tone (Professional, Casual, Friendly…) or translate it, with no prompt writing.

The **Try again** button resends the user’s original question and context, flagged with `regenerate: true`. This works for any backend, including ones that return images instead of text. With `aiAssistEndpoint`, the flag is sent in the request body as `regenerate`, and you can rename it through `aiAssistDataKeys`.

## Plugin Options

Each option links to its entry in [Options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/), with an example.

| Option | Type | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`aiSupplementalTermsAccepted`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSupplementalTermsAccepted) | Boolean | To use AI features in Froala, you need to accept the [AI Supplemental Terms](https://www.ideracorp.com/legal/Froala#tabs-2) by setting this option to true in your configuration. Defaults to `false`. |
| [`aiAssistEndpoint`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistEndpoint) | String \| null | The API endpoint URL for AI requests. Required if not using a custom request handler. Defaults to `null`. |
| [`aiAssistHeaders`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistHeaders) | Object | Additional HTTP headers to include with AI requests (e.g., authentication tokens). Defaults to `{}`. |
| [`aiAssistDataKeys`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistDataKeys) | Object \| null | Custom mapping for request data keys. Use this to match your API’s expected field names. Defaults to `null`. |
| [`aiAssistAdditionalData`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistAdditionalData) | Object \| null | Additional custom data fields to include in the request payload. Defaults to `null`. |
| [`aiAssistResponseParserPath`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistResponseParserPath) | String \| null | Path to extract the AI response from the API response object. Supports dot notation and array indexing. Defaults to `null`. |
| [`aiAssistToneOptions`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistToneOptions) | Array | Defines the available tone adjustment options in the AI Shortcuts dropdown. |
| [`aiAssistTranslateOptions`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistTranslateOptions) | Array | Defines the available translation languages in the AI Shortcuts dropdown. |
| [`aiAssistPromptTemplate`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistPromptTemplate) | String | The base template/instructions prepended to the requests of the AI Assist popup, its tone and translate shortcuts and the AI Chat panel. Improve Writing and inline suggestions send `aiImproveWritingPrompt` and `inlineSuggestionsPromptTemplate` instead. |
| [`aiChatWebSearchEnabled`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatWebSearchEnabled) | Boolean | Sets whether the web-search toggle in the AI Chat panel starts on or off. If the selected model in `aiChatModels` declares `webSearch: false`, the toggle stays off and disabled, and `webSearchEnabled` is removed from that model’s requests. Defaults to `false`. |
| [`aiChatModels`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatModels) | Array | Defines the list of selectable AI models shown in the chat panel’s model dropdown. Defaults to `[]`. |
| [`aiChatDefaultModel`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatDefaultModel) | String \| null | Sets which model from `aiChatModels` is preselected when the panel opens. Defaults to `null`. |
| [`aiChatReasoningEnabled`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatReasoningEnabled) | Boolean | Sets whether the reasoning toggle in the AI Chat panel starts on or off. If the selected model declares `reasoning: false`, the toggle stays off and disabled, and `reasoningEnabled` is removed from that model’s requests. Defaults to `false`. |
| [`aiChatStreamResponse`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatStreamResponse) | Boolean | Determines whether AI Chat answers stream in gradually or appear all at once. Defaults to `true`. |
| [`aiChatSupportedFileTypes`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatSupportedFileTypes) | Array | Lists the file extensions users can attach as AI Chat context. Defaults to `['pdf', 'docx', 'txt', 'md', 'jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp']`. |
| [`aiChatMaxFileSizeMB`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatMaxFileSizeMB) | Number | Sets the maximum size, in MB, allowed for a single attached file. Defaults to `20`. |
| [`aiChatMaxFiles`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatMaxFiles) | Number | Caps how many files can be attached to one AI Chat conversation. Defaults to `10`. |
| [`aiChatRequestTimeoutMs`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatRequestTimeoutMs) | Number | Sets how long, in milliseconds, to wait for an AI Chat response before timing out. Defaults to `60000`. |
| [`aiChatIncludeReferenceUrlsInContext`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatIncludeReferenceUrlsInContext) | Boolean | Controls whether “Reference URL” context sources are also folded into the outgoing prompt text. Defaults to `true`. |
| [`aiChatPanelWidth`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatPanelWidth) | Number \| null | Sets the initial width, in pixels, of the AI Chat panel. Defaults to `null`. |
| [`aiChatPanelMaxWidth`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatPanelMaxWidth) | Number \| null | Sets the maximum width, in pixels, the AI Chat panel can be resized to. Defaults to `null`, which allows 640px. |
| [`aiChatWelcomeMessage`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatWelcomeMessage) | String \| null | Overrides the intro text shown in the AI Chat panel’s empty-state welcome message. Defaults to `null`. |
| [`aiImproveWritingPrompt`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiImproveWritingPrompt) | String | The instruction sent to the AI backend whenever Improve Writing runs. Defaults to `'Rewrite the following content to fix spelling and grammar mistakes and improve clarity, using clear and professional language, while preserving the original meaning. Return only the rewritten plain text with no HTML tags, no markdown, and no extra commentary.'` |
| [`selectionActionButtons`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#selectionActionButtons) | Array | Lists the command buttons shown in the popup that appears when text is selected. Defaults to `['aiImproveWriting', 'collabAddComment']`. |
| [`inlineSuggestions`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#inlineSuggestions) | Boolean | Enables Gmail-style inline “ghost text” continuation suggestions while typing. Defaults to `true`. |
| [`inlineSuggestionsDelay`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#inlineSuggestionsDelay) | Number | Sets the debounce delay, in milliseconds, before an inline suggestion is requested. Defaults to `120`. |
| [`inlineSuggestionsPromptTemplate`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#inlineSuggestionsPromptTemplate) | String | The prompt template sent to the AI model to generate an inline continuation suggestion. Defaults to `'The text below is unfinished and the writer is about to keep typing. Continue it with a short natural phrase (a few words) made of whole, complete words. Ignore whether the last word already looks finished or not - never continue by adding more letters onto the end of it; always continue with a new, separate, complete word instead. Do not end with a period, question mark, or exclamation mark unless the sentence is clearly complete. Output only the continuation - no repetition, quotes, or markdown. If nothing fits, output nothing.'` |
| [`aiSpeechToText`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToText) | Boolean | Shows a microphone button letting users dictate their AI prompt instead of typing it. Defaults to `true`. |
| [`aiSpeechToTextWaveform`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToTextWaveform) | Boolean | Shows an animated “Listening…” waveform in place of the prompt input while recording. Defaults to `true`. |
| [`aiSpeechToTextListeningText`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToTextListeningText) | String | The label shown next to the recording waveform. Defaults to `'Listening'`. |
| [`aiSpeechToTextMaxDuration`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToTextMaxDuration) | Number | Sets the maximum recording duration, in seconds, before transcription is triggered automatically. Defaults to `120`. |
| [`aiAssistRequest`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistRequest) | Function \| null | Custom function to handle AI requests. It can stream through a third argument, `onChunk`, and report `webSearchUsed` in what it returns. Defaults to `null`. |

## Plugin Methods

Each method links to its entry in [Methods](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/), with an example.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`aiAssist.showPromptPopup()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiAssist.showPromptPopup) returns `void` | Opens the AI Assist prompt popup, allowing users to enter custom prompts for AI content generation. |
| [`aiChatAssistant.togglePanel()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiChatAssistant.togglePanel) returns `void` | Opens the AI Chat panel if it is closed, or closes it if it is open. |
| [`aiChatAssistant.isPanelOpen()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiChatAssistant.isPanelOpen) returns `Boolean` | Returns whether the AI Chat panel is currently open. |
| [`aiChatAssistant.sendMessage(text)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiChatAssistant.sendMessage) returns `void` | Sends a free-form prompt using the currently active context sources and the current web-search/model/reasoning state. `text` (String) is the message to send. |
| [`aiChatAssistant.addContextSource(source)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiChatAssistant.addContextSource) returns `Object \| Promise<Object>` | Adds a context source to the active conversation and returns its resolved descriptor. `source` (Object) is a descriptor of the shape `{ type: 'document' \| 'file' \| 'url', file?: File, url?: string }`. |
| [`aiChatAssistant.removeContextSource(id)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiChatAssistant.removeContextSource) returns `void` | Removes a previously added context source. `id` (String) is the id of the context source to remove. |
| [`aiChatAssistant.hasActiveConversation()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiChatAssistant.hasActiveConversation) returns `Boolean` | Returns whether the AI Chat panel currently has an active conversation. |
| [`aiChatAssistant.applyToEditor(messageId)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiChatAssistant.applyToEditor) returns `void` | Applies a given chat response’s text back into the document. `messageId` (String) is the id of the chat message whose content should be applied. |
| [`aiChatAssistant.getChatHistory()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiChatAssistant.getChatHistory) returns `Array` | Returns the complete AI Chat conversation so far, oldest turn first, as plain serializable records. |
| [`aiImproveWriting.applyExternalRewriteDirect(range, originalText, answer)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiImproveWriting.applyExternalRewriteDirect) returns `Boolean` | Applies an externally-generated rewrite using the same word-diff/review logic as Improve Writing itself, returning false if the editor is busy or the range has gone stale. `range` (Range) is a live DOM Range pointing at the region of content that `answer` replaces, captured before the request was sent. `originalText` (String) is the plain text that `range` contained when the request was sent, used to detect stale content and as the diff’s before side. `answer` (String) is the rewritten text returned by the AI backend, forming the diff’s after side. |
| [`aiAssist.requestAnswer(params, signal)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiAssist.requestAnswer) returns `Promise<Object>` | Sends a single buffered request to the AI backend and resolves with `{ answer, session_id?, webSearchUsed? }`. `params` (Object) is the request payload, also accepting the optional `webSearchEnabled`, `model`, `reasoningEnabled`, `files`, `referenceUrls`, and `regenerate` fields. `signal` (AbortSignal) is used to cancel an in-flight request. |
| [`aiAssist.requestAnswerStream(params, onChunk, signal)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiAssist.requestAnswerStream) returns `Promise<Object>` | Streaming sibling of `requestAnswer`, delivering raw text deltas through `onChunk` and resolving with `{ answer, session_id?, webSearchUsed? }`. `params` (Object) has the same shape as `requestAnswer`’s params. `webSearchEnabled` and `reasoningEnabled` are removed for a model that declares that capability `false`. `onChunk` (Function) is called with each decoded text chunk as it streams in. `signal` (AbortSignal) is used to cancel an in-flight request. |
| [`aiImproveWriting.start()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiImproveWriting.start) returns `void` | Sends the current selection to the AI and opens the appropriate review UI. |
| [`aiImproveWriting.hasActiveSession()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiImproveWriting.hasActiveSession) returns `Boolean` | Returns whether a standalone (non-collaborative) review session is currently open. |
| [`aiImproveWriting.isInFlight()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiImproveWriting.isInFlight) returns `Boolean` | Returns whether an Improve Writing request is currently waiting for a response. |
| [`aiImproveWriting.hasActiveCollabReview()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiImproveWriting.hasActiveCollabReview) returns `Boolean` | Returns whether the collaboration-aware review popup is currently open. |
| [`aiImproveWriting.acceptAllSession()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiImproveWriting.acceptAllSession) returns `void` | Accepts every pending change in the active standalone review session and ends it. |
| [`aiImproveWriting.rejectAllSession()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#aiImproveWriting.rejectAllSession) returns `void` | Rejects every pending change in the active standalone review session, restoring the original content, and ends it. |
| [`dockPanel.registerCoexistence(id, handlers)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#dockPanel.registerCoexistence) returns `void` | Registers a panel for “only one right-docked panel open at a time” coordination with other registered panels. `id` (String) is a unique id for the panel. `handlers` (Object) is `{ isOpen: () => boolean, hide: () => void }`. |
| [`dockPanel.unregisterCoexistence(id)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#dockPanel.unregisterCoexistence) returns `void` | Unregisters a panel previously registered with `registerCoexistence`. `id` (String) is the id passed to `registerCoexistence`. |

## Plugin Events

Each event links to its entry in [Events](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/), with an example. In a handler, `this` is the editor.

| Event | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`aiAssist.beforeInsert(responseContent)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.beforeInsert) | Triggered before AI-generated content is inserted into the editor. Returning `false` cancels the insert. `responseContent` is the HTML content about to be inserted. |
| [`aiAssist.afterInsert()`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.afterInsert) | Triggered after AI-generated content has been successfully inserted into the editor. |
| [`aiAssist.chatPanelResized(payload)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.chatPanelResized) | Fires after the user finishes drag-resizing the AI Chat panel. `payload` is an object with the new panel `width` in pixels. |
| [`aiAssist.chatBeforeApply(content)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.chatBeforeApply) | Fires before a chat response is inserted into the document; returning `false` cancels the insert. `content` is the text about to be inserted. |
| [`aiAssist.chatAfterApply`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.chatAfterApply) | Fires after a chat response has been inserted into the document. |
| [`aiAssist.improveWritingStarted`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.improveWritingStarted) | Fires when an Improve Writing request is sent to the AI backend. |
| [`aiAssist.improveWritingResponse(answer)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.improveWritingResponse) | Fires when the AI response for an Improve Writing request is received. `answer` is the raw rewritten text returned by the AI. |
| [`aiAssist.reviewStarted(sessionId)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.reviewStarted) | Fires when a standalone review session opens for AI-suggested changes. `sessionId` is the identifier for the review session. |
| [`aiAssist.hunkResolved(payload)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.hunkResolved) | Fires whenever a single change in the active review session is accepted or rejected. `payload` is an object with the resolved `changeId` and the `action` taken. |
| [`aiAssist.reviewEnded(sessionId)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.reviewEnded) | Fires when a review session ends because every change has been resolved. `sessionId` is the identifier for the review session. |
| [`aiAssist.beforeHunkInsert(payload)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.beforeHunkInsert) | Fires once per AI-proposed change during a collaborative Suggesting-mode review. `payload` is an object with the `range` the change applies to and the `hunk` describing it. |
| [`dockPanel.opening(id)`](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#dockPanel.opening) | Fires when a registered dock panel is about to become visible. `id` is the id of the panel that is opening. |

## Dependencies

The AI Assist plugin has **no required dependencies**. One feature has an optional one, Mammoth.js, only for DOCX file context.

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mammoth@1.11.0/mammoth.browser.js"></script>
```

If your users will attach **.docx** files as AI Chat context, load Mammoth.js before the editor’s scripts. It converts Word documents into HTML in the browser. It’s the same library the Import from Word plugin uses, and AI Chat finds it through that plugin’s `importFromWordMammoth` option, so with that plugin or the `pkgd` bundle you’re covered. With the AI Assist plugin alone, set the option yourself.

```js
new FroalaEditor('#editor', {
  aiSupplementalTermsAccepted: true,
  importFromWordMammoth: window.mammoth
});
```

## Add Plugin to Your Code

The plugin name is `aiAssist`. If you’re not using the `pkgd` bundle, include these two files individually, after the editor’s own.

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/plugins/ai_assist.min.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/ai_assist.min.js"></script>
```

With npm, import them after the editor.

```js
import FroalaEditor from 'froala-editor';
import 'froala-editor/css/plugins/ai_assist.min.css';
import 'froala-editor/js/plugins/ai_assist.min.js';
```

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Action | Windows and Linux | Mac |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open AI Assist popup | `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `I` | `⌘ Cmd` + `⇧ Shift` + `I` |

## Toolbar Buttons

| Button | Name |
| --- | --- |
| Open AI Assist popup | `aiAssist` |
| Open AI dropdown | `aiShortCuts` |
| Open or close the AI Chat panel | `aiChatAssistant` |

The default `toolbarButtons` has all three in its `moreRich` group.

With `toolbarInline`, the AI buttons are hidden and the shortcut does nothing.

## Quick Start Guide

Froala doesn’t ship with an AI model. You choose the provider, and one function connects it to the editor. This guide walks you through it end to end, with a small Node server that keeps your API key out of the browser, an editor page wired up in about 15 lines of config, and a working AI Chat panel you can talk to. No prior backend experience needed.

- [Explore Our Quick Start Guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/ai-assist-plugin/quick-start/)

## Examples

- [Direct OpenAI API Integration](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/examples/ai-assist-direct-openai-api-integration/)
- [Custom Backend with Validation + Event Hooks](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/examples/ai-assist-custom-backend-with-validation-event-hooks/)
- [Standard Endpoint with Custom Request/Response Format](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/examples/ai-assist-standard-endpoint-with-custom-request-response-format/)

## Additional Resources

- [Stream AI Answers Into Froala Through Your Own Server](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/stream-ai-answers-froala-own-server/)
- [Setup AI React WYSIWYG Editor Powered by Claude](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/ai-react-wysiwyg-editor-claude/)
- [How to Set Up Froala with DeepSeek AI Assist in WordPress](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/froala-deepseek-ai-wordpress-setup/)

pages.markdown:
# Align Plugin

-   [Methods](#methods "Methods")
-   [Examples](#examples "Examples")

Align plugin will add these buttons and functionality to Froala editor:

-   Align Left.
-   Align Center.
-   Align Right.
-   Align Justify.

These buttons will display by default at the More paragraph menu.

  

## Plugin methods:

[**align.apply (value)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#align.apply)

[**align.refresh ($btn)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#align.refresh)

pages.title: Char Counter Plugin
pages.markdown:
# Char Counter Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Methods](#methods "Methods")
-   [Events](#events "Events")
-   [Examples](#examples "Examples")

Display the number of characters at the bottom bar of the editor and will be updated with every character you add or remove. Also, it allows you to limit the number of characters that a user can enter in the editor.

  

## Plugin options:

[**charCounterCount**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#charCounterCount)  
Boolean - Default: True

Enables or disables the display of the character counter.

[**charCounterMax**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#charCounterMax)  
Number - Default: -1

The maximum number of characters allowed to be inserted into the rich text editor. -1 means that there is no limit set.

  

## Plugin methods:

[**charCounter.count()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#charCounter.count)  
returns: Integer

Returns the number of characters in the editor.

  

## Plugin events:

pages.title: Collaborative Plugin
pages.markdown:
# Collaborative Plugin

The **Froala Collaboration Plugin** brings enterprise-grade collaborative editing features directly to the Froala WYSIWYG Editor.

## Real-time editing:

Live Syncing keeps every editor instance perfectly in sync in real time. When one user types, all other open instances update instantly — no refresh needed, no conflicts.

A Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT) engine resolves concurrent edits. Presence indicators show active cursors. WebSocket transport delivers sub-100ms latency.

## Suggestion Mode Editing:

Writers or reviewers propose changes —  insertions, deletions, or rewrites — without directly altering the live document. Document owners accept or reject each suggestion individually or in bulk.

## Comments:

Highlight any text and attach a threaded comment. Collaborators reply inline, resolve discussions, and @mention teammates — all anchored to the exact content being discussed.

With comments users can:

-   Threaded replies per comment anchor
-   @mention to notify specific users
-   Resolve / reopen discussion threads
-   Comments sidebar with full thread view
-   Filter: open, resolved, by author

## Version Control:

View, compare, and restore previous document versions.

Users can

-   Browse: Scroll through timestamped snapshots with author attribution
-   Compare: Side-by-side diff of any two versions
-   Restore: One-click rollback to any prior state, no data loss
-   Audit: Full author + timestamp log for compliance requirements

> Real-time collaboration and persistence require a backend server. The Collaborative backend ships in the wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk package and is split into four modules: a WebSocket relay for real-time peer sync, REST endpoints for comments and suggestions, a version history store, and an async content-save endpoint. All four can share a single HTTP server and a single SQLite file, and the required better-sqlite3 dependency installs automatically with the package. [See Backend API Reference](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/collaborative-plugin/collaborative-backend-api-reference/)

## Plugin API
