pages.title: Collaborative Backend API Reference
pages.markdown:
# Collaborative Backend API Reference Four independent modules power [Froala’s collaboration plugin](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/collaborative-plugin/): a real-time WebSocket relay, plus REST + SQLite stores for suggestions & comments, version snapshots, and offline saves. Mount only what you need — or run all four on a single HTTP server and a single database file. System at a glance Browser peer Froala + Yjs Browser peer Froala + Yjs Browser peer Froala + Yjs SINGLE HTTP SERVER · PORT 3000 01 Collaborative WebSocket relay · broadcast by docId 02 CollabPersistence suggestions · comments 03 Version Control snapshots 04 AsyncSave offline content upsert collab.db SQLite ## Overview The collaborative backend is split across four modules that you compose as needed: a **WebSocket relay** for real-time peer sync, **REST endpoints** for persisting suggestions and comments, a **version history store**, and an **async content-save endpoint** for offline mode. All four can share a single HTTP server and a single SQLite file. Module File Responsibility Collaborative lib/collaborative.js Pure WebSocket relay. Broadcasts messages between peers of the same document. CollabPersistence lib/collab\_persistence.js REST + SQLite for track-change suggestions and inline comments. VersionControl lib/version\_control.js REST + SQLite for named or auto snapshots of document content. AsyncSave lib/async\_save.js REST + SQLite for saving/loading the latest content in offline (async) mode. ## Getting started ### Install The four modules ship as part of the [Froala Node.js SDK](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/nodejs/). bash ``` npm install wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk ``` SQLite dependency `CollabPersistence`, `VersionControl`, and `AsyncSave` require `better-sqlite3`. It ships as a regular dependency and installs automatically — no separate step needed. **Body parsing:** All four modules read parsed request bodies from `req.body`. Mount both Express body parsers before calling any `attachRoutes` method. The collaboration plugin sends comments, suggestions and versions as JSON, while the save plugin sends document content form-encoded, so a server with only `express.json()` will reject every content save with `400 Bad Request`. JavaScript ``` app.use(express.json({ limit: '5mb' })); app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true, limit: '5mb' })); ``` The default 100kb limit is too small for version snapshots, which contain the full document. Raise it to match your largest realistic document. ### Import the modules All collaborative modules are exported from the package’s main entry point. Destructure the ones you need: javascript · commonjs ``` const FroalaEditor = require('wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk'); const Collaborative = FroalaEditor.Collaborative; const CollabPersistence = FroalaEditor.CollabPersistence; const VersionControl = FroalaEditor.VersionControl; const AsyncSave = FroalaEditor.AsyncSave; ``` ## Conventions Every REST endpoint is namespaced under `/collab/:docId/`. The `:docId` segment identifies the collaborative document and **must match the `docId` used by the WebSocket connection**. Document IDs are arbitrary strings; URL-encode any characters outside `a-z 0-9 - _`. Transport URL pattern WS ws:///{docId} REST http:///collab/{docId}/{resource} ## Full server example The most common setup runs the relay and all three REST stores on one Express-wrapped HTTP server, backed by one shared SQLite file. This wires everything together end to end: javascript · server.js ``` const http = require('http'); const express = require('express'); const path = require('path'); const { Collaborative, CollabPersistence, VersionControl, AsyncSave, } = require('wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk'); const app = express(); app.use(express.json()); // One SQLite file shared by all three persistence modules const dbPath = path.join(__dirname, 'data', 'collab.db'); CollabPersistence.attachRoutes(app, { dbPath }); VersionControl.attachRoutes(app, { dbPath }); AsyncSave.attachRoutes(app, { dbPath }); // Optional: expose live relay stats on the shared server app.get('/health', (req, res) => res.json(Collaborative.getStats())); // Share ONE HTTP server between REST and the WebSocket relay const server = http.createServer(app); Collaborative.attachToServer(server); server.listen(3000, () => { console.log('Collaborative backend on http://localhost:3000'); }); ``` Why attachToServer? Use `attachToServer()` (not `createServer()`) whenever REST endpoints and the relay must live on the same port. `createServer()` is for running the relay as the _only_ service on a port. ## Module 01 — Collaborative lib/collaborative.js · WebSocket relay A pure WebSocket relay server. It groups connections by `docId` and broadcasts every incoming message to all _other_ members of that document. **All collaboration logic lives in the browser clients** — the server never parses or validates message content. A keepalive heartbeat pings every 30 s and terminates any client that fails to pong within 10 s. FN Collaborative.createServer(options?) Creates a self-contained HTTP + WebSocket server. The HTTP side answers `GET /health` and rejects all other HTTP requests with `426 Upgrade Required`. Use it when the relay is the only service on the port. Parameter Type Description options object optional Configuration object. options.port number optional Port to listen on. Default: `3000`. **Returns** — `WebSocket.Server`, the underlying `ws` instance. javascript ``` const { Collaborative } = require('wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk'); // Starts on port 3000; clients connect to ws://localhost:3000/{docId} const wss = Collaborative.createServer({ port: 3000 }); ``` FN Collaborative.attachToServer(httpServer) Attaches the relay to an existing HTTP (or Express-wrapped) server. Use it when REST endpoints and the relay must share one port. Parameter Type Description httpServer http.Server required A Node.js `http.Server` instance (including those created by Express). **Returns** — `WebSocket.Server`. javascript · express + shared port ``` const http = require('http'); const express = require('express'); const { Collaborative } = require('wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk'); const app = express(); const server = http.createServer(app); Collaborative.attachToServer(server); server.listen(3000); ``` FN Collaborative.setupWSConnection(conn, req) Low-level handler that wires a single connection into the document registry. Called automatically by both `createServer` and `attachToServer` — use it directly only when managing your own `ws` server. Parameter Type Description conn WebSocket required The incoming connection from the `connection` event. req http.IncomingMessage required The HTTP upgrade request. The document ID is derived from `req.url`: the leading slash is removed and the path before the first `?` is URL-decoded. Falls back to `default-doc` if the path is empty. **Returns** — `void`. Document lifecycle A document entry is created when the first client joins and deleted when the last client disconnects. Clients that join an empty document receive **no historical state** — they must wait for another peer to reconnect and push a sync message. FN Collaborative.getStats() Returns a snapshot of server state: active document count and total open connections. returns ``` { "docs": 3, "clients": 7 } ``` GET /health Live document and client counts. Available on the standalone server from `createServer()`. With `attachToServer()`, add this route yourself using `Collaborative.getStats()`. **200** OK json ``` { "docs": 3, "clients": 7 } ``` WS ws:/// Connect to a collaborative document. The path after the leading slash is the URL-decoded document ID. Every text or binary message from one client is relayed **verbatim** to all other clients in the same document. Segment Type Description docId string required Identifies the document. All clients on the same `docId` are peers. URL-encoded; decoded by the server before grouping. An empty path defaults to `default-doc`. Relay semantics The server is a transparent relay: it does not store messages or replay history to late joiners. All CRDT/OT state, cursor sync, and protocol versioning are the client’s responsibility — Froala’s collaborative plugin uses **Yjs** internally. Message size limit Any message larger than **1 MB** is silently dropped and never forwarded to peers. Keep individual sync messages well below this threshold. javascript · browser client ``` // Connect to document "my-doc-2024" const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:3000/my-doc-2024'); ws.addEventListener('message', (event) => { // Handle incoming sync messages from other peers handleCollabMessage(event.data); }); // Send a message — relayed to all other peers in the document ws.send(encodeUpdate(myUpdate)); ``` ## Module 02 — CollabPersistence lib/collab\_persistence.js · REST + SQLite REST endpoints backed by SQLite for persisting track-change **suggestions** and inline **comments** per document. Anchor positions are stored as opaque JSON strings — the server never interprets editor-internal position data. FN CollabPersistence.attachRoutes(app, options?) Registers all suggestion and comment routes on an Express app and initialises the SQLite tables on first call. Parameter Type Description app Express required An Express application instance. options.dbPath string optional Path to the SQLite file. Default: `collab.db` (relative to the process CWD). Created if it doesn’t exist. javascript ``` const path = require('path'); const { CollabPersistence } = require('wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk'); CollabPersistence.attachRoutes(app, { dbPath: path.join(__dirname, 'data', 'collab.db') }); ``` ### Suggestions Track-change suggestions created by collaborators. Each records the original and proposed text, the editor position (anchor), the author, and a lifecycle status. GET /collab/:docId/suggestions Returns all suggestions for a document, ordered by timestamp ascending. The `replies` field is _not_ included in the list response. Path param Type Description docId string required Document identifier. **200** OK — array of suggestion objects **Suggestion object schema** json ``` { "id": "sug-001", "doc_id": "demo-doc", "type": "insert", // operation type (opaque to server) "author_id": "user-42", "author_name": "Alice", "timestamp": 1720000000000, // Unix milliseconds "original_text": "Hello world", "suggested_text": "Hello everyone", "anchor_start": "[0,5]", // JSON-serialised position array "anchor_end": "[0,16]", // JSON-serialised position array "status": "pending" // "pending" | "accepted" | "rejected" } ``` Anchors `anchor_start` and `anchor_end` are stored and returned as JSON strings. Run `JSON.parse` if you need the underlying position array. POST /collab/:docId/suggestions Creates a new suggestion. A `409` should be treated as confirmation the suggestion was already persisted. Field Type Description id string required Unique identifier, generated by the client. type string required Operation type (e.g. `insert`, `delete`, `format`). Opaque to the server. authorId string optional Stored as `author_id`. authorName string optional Stored as `author_name`. timestamp number optional Unix ms. Defaults to server time (`Date.now()`). originalText string optional Stored as `original_text`. suggestedText string optional Stored as `suggested_text`. anchor object optional Position object with `start` and `end`. Each is JSON-serialised into `anchor_start` / `anchor_end`. status string optional One of `pending`, `accepted`, `rejected`. Default: `pending`. **201** Created **400** missing id or type **409** id already exists json · request body ``` { "id": "sug-001", "type": "insert", "authorId": "user-42", "authorName": "Alice", "originalText": "Hello world", "suggestedText": "Hello everyone", "anchor": { "start": [0, 5], "end": [0, 16] } } ``` json · 201 response ``` { "id": "sug-001" } ``` PATCH /collab/:docId/suggestions/:id Updates the status and/or replies of a suggestion. At least one field must be present. Field Type Description status string optional One of `pending`, `accepted`, `rejected`. An invalid value returns `400`. replies array optional Full replacement array of reply objects, JSON-serialised before storage. Pass `[]` to clear. **200** OK **400** empty body / invalid status json · response variants ``` // when status is updated { "id": "sug-001", "status": "accepted" } // when only replies is updated { "id": "sug-001" } ``` DELETE /collab/:docId/suggestions/:id Permanently deletes a suggestion. Returns `204` whether or not the suggestion existed (idempotent). **204** No Content ### Comments Inline comments anchored to a position in the document. Comments support a `resolved` flag and a `replies` list. GET /collab/:docId/comments Returns all comments for a document, ordered by timestamp ascending. The `replies` field is not included in the list response. **200** OK — array of comment objects json · comment schema ``` { "id": "cmt-001", "doc_id": "demo-doc", "author_id": "user-42", "author_name": "Alice", "timestamp": 1720000000000, "text": "Should we rephrase this paragraph?", "anchor_start": "[1,0]", // JSON-serialised position array "anchor_end": "[1,42]", "resolved": 0 // 0 = unresolved, 1 = resolved (integer) } ``` Type note `resolved` is returned as an **integer** (0 or 1), not a boolean. `anchor_start` / `anchor_end` are JSON strings — parse them as needed. POST /collab/:docId/comments Creates a new comment. A `409` confirms the comment was already persisted. Field Type Description id string required Unique identifier, generated by the client. authorId string optional Author’s unique identifier. authorName string optional Author’s display name. timestamp number optional Unix ms. Defaults to server time. text string optional Comment body. Default: `""`. anchor object optional Position with `start` and `end`. Each is JSON-serialised. resolved boolean optional Default: `false`. Stored as integer 0/1. replies array optional Initial reply objects. Default: `[]`. JSON-serialised before storage. **201** Created **400** missing id **409** id already exists json · 201 response ``` { "id": "cmt-001" } ``` PATCH /collab/:docId/comments/:id Updates the resolved state and/or replies. At least one field must be present. Field Type Description resolved boolean optional Truthy values stored as 1, falsy as 0. replies array optional Full replacement array. Pass `[]` to clear. **200** OK **400** neither field present **404** comment not found json · 200 response ``` { "id": "cmt-001" } ``` DELETE /collab/:docId/comments/:id Permanently deletes a comment. **204** No Content ## Module 03 — VersionControl lib/version\_control.js · REST + SQLite REST endpoints backed by SQLite for storing named or auto-generated snapshots of editor content per document. Each snapshot captures the full document state at a point in time and is optionally annotated with a title and description. Versions are **append-only** — they cannot be edited in content, only renamed. FN VersionControl.attachRoutes(app, options?) Registers version-control routes on an Express app and initialises the `versions` table on first call. Parameter Type Description app Express required An Express application instance. options.dbPath string optional SQLite file path. Default: `collab.db`. Can share the same file as the other modules. GET /collab/:docId/versions Returns all version summaries for a document, ordered by `created_at` descending (newest first). The `snapshot` field is excluded for performance — use the single-version endpoint to retrieve it. **200** OK — array of version summaries json · version summary (no snapshot) ``` { "id": "rv-lp8k3a2-9xf2r", "doc_id": "demo-doc", "title": "Before major refactor", // null if unnamed "description": null, "created_at": 1720000000000, "author_id": "user-42", "author_name": "Alice", "is_named": 1, // 1 if title is set, 0 otherwise "source": "manual" // "manual" | "auto" } ``` GET /collab/:docId/versions/:id Returns a single version including the full `snapshot` field. **200** OK — full version object **404** Not Found json · full version ``` { "id": "rv-lp8k3a2-9xf2r", "doc_id": "demo-doc", "title": "Before major refactor", "description": null, "snapshot": "

Document content here

", "created_at": 1720000000000, "author_id": "user-42", "author_name": "Alice", "is_named": 1, "source": "manual" } ``` POST /collab/:docId/versions Creates a new snapshot. If `id` is omitted, the server generates one as `rv-{base36timestamp}-{random}`. Field Type Description snapshot string required Full document content (HTML string for Froala). id string optional Client-supplied identifier. Auto-generated if absent. title string optional Human-readable name. When non-empty, sets `is_named = 1`. description string optional Longer description or change notes. author object optional Author info. `author.id` → `author_id`, `author.name` → `author_name`. source string optional `auto` for periodic auto-saves; anything else stored as `manual`. Default: `manual`. Server-controlled timestamp The server always records the current time as `created_at`. Any `createdAt` field in the request body is ignored. **201** Created — `{ id }` only **400** missing snapshot **409** id already exists json · request body ``` { "snapshot": "

Document content here

", "title": "Before major refactor", "author": { "id": "user-42", "name": "Alice" }, "source": "manual" } ``` PATCH /collab/:docId/versions/:id Updates the title and/or description. Snapshot content cannot be changed. At least one field is required. Field Type Description title string | null optional New title. Pass `null` to clear (sets `is_named = 0`). A non-empty string sets `is_named = 1`. description string | null optional New description. Pass `null` to clear. **200** OK — updated full version **400** neither field present **404** Not Found DELETE /collab/:docId/versions/:id Permanently deletes a version snapshot. **204** No Content ## Module 04 — AsyncSave lib/async\_save.js · REST + SQLite REST endpoints for saving and loading the latest editor content per document. Used when the editor runs in **async (offline) mode**. In real-time mode this endpoint is still required if comment and suggestion highlights are to survive a reload. The comment and suggestion records come from `commentsUrl` and `suggestionsUrl`, but their anchors resolve against the document content, which is stored here. A document that is never saved will load its comment cards with nothing to attach them to — i.e. when `collabConfig.realTime.syncUrl` is not set. Each document has exactly one content row; every POST upserts the current state. FN AsyncSave.attachRoutes(app, options?) Registers the async-save routes on an Express app and initialises the `async_content` table on first call. Parameter Type Description app Express required An Express application instance. options.dbPath string optional SQLite file path. Default: `collab.db`. Can share the same file as the other modules. POST /collab/:docId/content Saves (upserts) the current editor HTML. Each document has exactly one content row — repeated calls replace the previous value. Field Type Description body string required Full editor HTML to persist. Field name matches Froala’s default `saveParam`. authorId string optional Identifier of the user who performed the save. authorName string optional Display name of the user who performed the save. Field name The Froala save plugin sends its payload using the field name `body` (the default `saveParam`), encoded as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. This endpoint also accepts `application/json` if you post to it directly. Your server must have `express.urlencoded()` mounted to receive saves from the plugin. `400 Bad Request` — if the body field is missing. A request that looks correct in the browser’s network tab but returns 400 usually means the matching body parser is not mounted, so `req.body` arrived empty. **200** OK **400** missing body field json · request body ``` { "body": "

Updated document content.

", "authorId": "user-42", "authorName": "Alice" } ``` Save timing `saveInterval` is the minimum delay before a save is attempted, not a fixed cadence. The save plugin waits for a `contentChanged` event, then waits `saveInterval` milliseconds, then skips the request entirely if the content is unchanged since the last successful save. The observed gap between an edit and a request is therefore longer than `saveInterval` and varies with typing. `editor.save.force()` sets a flag so the next save is not skipped. It returns `undefined` and does not send a request. Use `editor.save.save()` to save immediately. For predictable persistence, save explicitly rather than relying on the interval JavaScript ``` events: { contentChanged: function () { const html = this.html.get(); clearTimeout(this._saveTimer); this._saveTimer = setTimeout(() => { fetch('/collab/my-doc/content', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ body: html }) }); }, 2000); } } ``` json · 200 response ``` { "doc_id": "demo-doc", "saved_at": 1720000000000 } ``` GET /collab/:docId/content Returns the most recently saved content for a document. Sanitization Content is returned **verbatim**. Sanitizing the HTML before rendering is the caller’s responsibility. **200** OK **404** no content saved json · 200 response ``` { "doc_id": "demo-doc", "content": "

Updated document content.

", "author_id": "user-42", "author_name": "Alice", "saved_at": 1720000000000 } ``` json · 404 response ``` { "error": "no content saved for this document" } ``` ## Error format All endpoints return errors as JSON with a single `error` field describing what went wrong. No envelope wrapping, no nested objects. json · error response ``` { "error": "id and type are required" } ``` Status When **400** A required field is missing or a value is invalid (e.g. an invalid `status` string, or an empty body on a PATCH endpoint). **404** The requested resource does not exist. **409** A resource with the supplied `id` already exists (POST suggestions, comments, versions). **500** An unexpected database or server error. The `error` field contains the underlying SQLite message. ## Still Have Questions? Here are some additional resources if you can’t find an answer you need. [Help Center](https://wysiwyg-editor.froala.help/hc/en-us)[Docs](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/getting-started/) [Contact Us](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/contact/)[Github](https://github.com/froala) [Blog](https://froala.com/blog/)[Case Studies](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/customers/)

pages.markdown:
# Colors Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Methods](#methods "Methods")
-   [Examples](#examples "Examples")

Adds the possibility to change the background and text colors. You can build your own color palette.

  

## Plugin options:

[**colorsBackground**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#colorsBackground)  
Array -

An array of colors used in the colors popup for background. Passing REMOVE as a value in the array will display the Clear Formatting button for colors.

* * *

**Default:**  
\[  
'#61BD6D', '#1ABC9C', '#54ACD2', '#2C82C9', '#9365B8', '#475577', '#CCCCCC',  
'#41A85F', '#00A885', '#3D8EB9', '#2969B0', '#553982', '#28324E', '#000000',  
'#F7DA64', '#FBA026', '#EB6B56', '#E25041', '#A38F84', '#EFEFEF', '#FFFFFF',,  
'#FAC51C', '#F37934', '#D14841', '#B8312F', '#7C706B', '#D1D5D8', 'REMOVE'  
\]

[**colorsButtons**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#colorsButtons)  
Array -

Set the colors popup buttons.

* * *

Default: \["colorsBack", "|", "-"\]

[**colorsHEXInput**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#colorsHEXInput)  
Boolean -

Show HEX input to choose custom color.

* * *

Default: true

[**colorsStep**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#colorsStep)  
Number -

The number of colors displayed on a line in the colors popup.

* * *

Default: 7

[**colorsText**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#colorsText)  
Array -

An array of colors used in the colors popup for text. Passing REMOVE as a value in the array will display the Clear Formatting button for colors.

* * *

Default:  
  
\[ '#61BD6D', '#1ABC9C', '#54ACD2', '#2C82C9', '#9365B8', '#475577', '#CCCCCC',  
'#41A85F', '#00A885', '#3D8EB9', '#2969B0', '#553982', '#28324E', '#000000',  
'#F7DA64', '#FBA026', '#EB6B56', '#E25041', '#A38F84', '#EFEFEF', '#FFFFFF',  
'#FAC51C', '#F37934', '#D14841', '#B8312F', '#7C706B', '#D1D5D8', 'REMOVE'  
\]

  

## Plugin methods:

[**colors.background (value)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#colors.background%0D%0A)  
returns: Object

Set the background color of the selected text.

* * *

**● Value:** The color to be set.  
Type: String

[**colors.text (value)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#colors.text%0D%0A)  
returns: Object

Set the text color of the selected text.

* * *

**● Value:** The color to be set.  
Type: String

[**colors.back ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#colors.back%0D%0A)  
returns:

Hides the color picker popup.

  

## Add Plugin to your code:

**Plugin name:** colors

**Plugin JS Script:** ../js/plugins/colors.min.js

Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/colors.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/colors.min.js)

**Plugin CSS link:** ../css/plugins/colors.min.css

Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/plugins/colors.min.css](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/plugins/colors.min.css)

pages.title: Embedly Plugin
pages.markdown:
# Embedly Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Methods](#methods "Methods")
-   [Events](#events "Events")
-   [Examples](#examples "Examples")

Embeds any content from the web in the editor.

  

## Plugin options:

[**embedlyKey**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#embedlyKey)  
String - Default: null

Your key from Embed.ly to remove the "Powered By Banner".

[**embedlyEditButtons**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#embedlyEditButtons)  
Array - Default: \['embedlyRemove'\]

The buttons that appear in the edit Embed.ly popup, when an embedded object is selected.

[**embedlyInsertButtons**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#embedlyInsertButtons)  
Array - Default: \['embedlyRemove'\]

The buttons that appear in the insert Embed.ly popup, when an embedded object is inserted into the WYSIWYG editor.

[**embedlyScriptPath**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#embedlyScriptPath)  
String - Default: The default script path for the Embedly JS.

The default script path for the Embedly JS.

  

## Plugin methods:

[**embedly.add (url)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#embedly.add)  
returns: .

Add the embedly to the editor.

* * *

**● Url:**URL for the embedly.  
Type: String

[**embedly.back ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#embedly.back)  
returns:

Hides the insert popup and shows an inline menu for the currently selected embedly.

[**embedly.get ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#embedly.get)  
returns:

Gets the currently embedly instance.

[**embedly.insert ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#embedly.insert)  
returns:

Inserts the embedly into the editor from the popup.

[**embedly.remove ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#embedly.remove)  
returns:

Removes the currently selected embedly instance.

[**embedly.showInsertPopup ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#embedly.showInsertPopup)  
returns:

Shows insert popup.

  

## Plugin events:

[**embedly.beforeRemove (embeded)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#embedly.beforeRemove)  
.

Triggered before the embedly embeded object is removed from editor.

* * *

**● embeded**  
Current embeded object to be removed.

  

## Add Plugin to your code:

**Plugin name:** embedly

**Plugin JS Script:** ../js/third\_party/embedly.min.js

Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/third\_party/embedly.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/third_party/embedly.min.js)

pages.title: Export to Word Plugin
pages.markdown:
# Export to Word Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Events](#events "Events")
-   [Dependence](#dependence "Dependence")

The Export to Word plugin enables users to export the editor’s content directly into a Microsoft Word (.docx) file. This feature is especially useful for scenarios where content needs to be shared, printed, or archived in a widely accepted document format.

  

## Plugin options:

[**wordExportFileName**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#wordExportFileName)  
String

Specifies the name of the file to be exported. The plugin automatically handles the file extension, so only the base name needs to be provided.

* * *

Default: 'NameOfTheFile'

  

## Plugin events:

[**word.beforeExport (editorHtml)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#word.beforeExport)

This event is triggered just before the export process begins. The editor’s HTML content is passed to the callback, allowing you to modify or inspect it before export.

* * *

**● editorHtml -** The HTML content of the editor prior to export.

[**word.afterExport (editorHtml)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#word.afterExport)

This event is triggered after the export process is completed. The exported HTML content of the editor is available through the callback.

* * *

**● editorHtml -** The HTML content of the editor at the time of export.

  

## Dependence

For the plugin to work properly, you need to include the file-saver and html-docx libraries in your project.

-   If you're working in a browser environment, you can include them via CDN.

pages.title: File Plugin
pages.markdown:
# File Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Methods](#methods "Methods")
-   [Events](#events "Events")
-   [Examples](#examples "Examples")

Upload any kind of files and special links will be inserted in the editor to download them. You can drag and drop any file to upload it or use the specially designed popup for handling file upload

  

## Plugin options:

[**fileAllowedTypes**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileAllowedTypes)  
Array - Default: \['\*'\]

The list of file types that are allowed to be uploaded. Although this will restrict uploading other types of files, we strongly recommend you to check the file type on the server too.

[**fileInsertButtons**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileInsertButtons)  
Array - Default: \['fileBack', '|'\]

The list of file types that are allowed to be uploaded. Although this will restrict uploading other types of files, we strongly recommend you to check the file type on the server too.

[**fileMaxSize**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileMaxSize)  
Number - Default: 1024 \* 1024 \* 10

The maximum file size allowed on upload in bytes. The default value is 10MB. Although this makes an additional check before uploading the file, it is highly recommended to check file size on your server too.

[**fileUpload**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileUpload)  
Boolean - Default: true

Enable or disable file upload.

[**fileUploadMethod**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileUploadMethod)  
String - Default: 'POST'

The HTTP file upload request type.

[**fileUploadParam**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileUploadParam)  
String - Default: 'file'

Customize the name of the parameter that contains the file in the upload request.

[**fileUploadParams**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileUploadParams)  
Object - Default: {}

Pass additional parameters to the file upload request.

[**fileUploadToS3**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileUploadToS3)  
Object - Default: false

Set the options for file upload to S3. All the fields from the example below are required. Also make sure that you have enabled CORS on Amazon.

[**fileUploadURL**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileUploadURL)  
String - Default:'http://i.froala.com/upload'

The URL where the files uploaded by the user are saved.

[**fileUseSelectedText**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fileUseSelectedText)  
Boolean - Default: false

Enables using the file's name instead of the selected text when a file is inserted.

  

## Plugin methods:

[**file.insert (link, , \[response\])**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#file.insert)  
returns: Object

Insert the link to a file at the cursor position.

* * *

**● link:**The link to the file.  
Type: String  
**● text:** The text for the file.  
Type: String  
**● response:** The response from the server.  
Type: String

[**file.upload (files)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#file.upload)  
returns: Object

Upload the passed file to the server.

* * *

**● files:** An array with the files to be uploaded to the server. It is usually the value of a file input.  
Type: Array

  

## Plugin events:

[**file.beforeUpload (files)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#file.beforeUpload)  

Triggered before uploading a file to the server.  
**Note:** Returning false in the handler assigned to the event will cancel the current action.

* * *

**● files:** An array with the files to be uploaded.

[**file.error (error, response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#file.error)  

Triggered after error occurs in uploading a file to the server.  
**Note:** Returning false in the handler assigned to the event will cancel the current action.

* * *

**● error** An object containing error code and description.  
**● response** Response object received from server.

[**file.inserted ($file, response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#file.inserted)  

Triggered after the request to upload a file has been completed successfully.

* * *

**● $file** A jQuery object with the inserted file.  
**● response** The original response from the server.

[**file.unlink (link)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#file.unlink)  

Triggered after removing a file link.  
**Note:** Returning false in the handler assigned to the event will cancel the current action.

* * *

**● link** A DOM Object with the link removed.

[**file.uploaded (response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#file.uploaded)  

Triggered after the file was uploaded.  
**Note:** Returning false in the handler assigned to the event will cancel the current action.

* * *

**● link** The original server response.

[**file.uploadedToS3 (link, key, response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#file.uploadedToS3)  

Triggered after the file was uploaded to S3.

* * *

**● link** The link to the uploaded file.  
**● key** The key of the uploaded file.  
**● response** The original server response.  

  

## Add Plugin to your code:

**Plugin name:** file

**Plugin JS Script:** ../js/plugins/file.min.js

Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/file.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/file.min.js)

**Plugin CSS link:** ../css/plugins/file.min.css

  

**Plugin CSS link** [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/plugins/file.min.css](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/plugins/file.min.css)

  
**Storing files on your server:**  
To store files on your server you may need to use one of the following [SDKs](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/)

## Example:

[Files upload handling](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/file/upload/)

## Additional Resources

-   [How to customize Froala Image Edit Buttons in a React App](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/how-to-customize-froala-image-edit-buttons-in-a-react-app/)
-   [Image Management in Express Framework: Froala Node.JS SDK](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/image-management-in-express-framework-froala-node-js-sdk/)
-   [Froala Image Management in Laravel: Easy for HTML Code Writers](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/simplify-froala-image-management-in-laravel-using-froala-html-code-writer/)

pages.title: Filerobot Image Editor (FIE) Plugin
pages.markdown:
# Filerobot Image Editor (FIE) Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Examples](#examples "Examples")

Adds integration with Filerobot Image Editor for advanced image editing inside Froala Editor. Users can open the selected image in Filerobot, apply edits such as annotations, filters, resize, rotate, watermark, and save the updated image back into the editor. The plugin automatically adds Advanced Edit inside imageEditButtons.

## Plugin options:

[**filerobotOptions**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#filerobotOptions) Object –

Configure the Filerobot Image Editor’s appearance and behavior such as theme, tools, default tabs, output type, and save settings.  
Default:  

```
{
  theme: {
    palette: {
      'bg-primary-active': '#4CA6FF'
    },
    typography: {
      fontFamily: 'Roboto, Arial'
    }
  },
  annotationsCommon: {
    fill: '#ff0000'
  },
  Text: { text: 'Enter text...' },
  Rotate: { angle: 90, componentType: 'buttons' },
  tabsIds: ['Adjust', 'Annotate', 'Filters', 'Finetune', 'Resize', 'Watermark'],
  defaultTabId: 'Annotate',
  defaultToolId: 'Text',
  savingPixelRatio: 0,
  previewPixelRatio: 0,
  closeAfterSave: true,
  defaultSavedImageType: 'png'
}
```

[**FilerobotImageEditor**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#filerobotOptions) Object

Used to provide the Filerobot Image Editor instance manually if not available globally.  
Default: `window.FilerobotImageEditor`

## Plugin events:

[**filerobot.beforeOpen()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filerobot.beforeOpen)

Triggered before opening the Filerobot editor.

[**filerobot.opened(filerobotInstance)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filerobot.opened)

Triggered after the Filerobot editor is rendered.

* * *

**● filerobotInstance (Object):** The code content to insert

[**filerobot.beforeSave(editedImageObject)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filerobot.beforeSave)

Triggered before saving the edited image.

* * *

**● editedImageObject (Object):** Contains image data

[**filerobot.saved (editedImageObject)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filerobot.saved)

Triggered after the edited image is uploaded successfully.

* * *

**● editedImageObject (Object):** Contains image data

[**filerobot.closed()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filerobot.closed)

Triggered after the Filerobot editor is closed or destroyed.

## Dependencies:

Include Filerobot Image Editor script in your page  
`<script src="https://scaleflex.cloudimg.io/v7/plugins/filerobot-image-editor/latest/filerobot-image-editor.min.js">`

## Add Plugin to your code:

**Plugin name:** imageFilerobot **Plugin JS Script:** ../js/third\_party/imageFileRobot.min.js Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/third\_party/imageFileRobot.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/third_party/imageFileRobot.min.js) **Plugin CSS link:** ../css/third\_party/imageFileRobot.min.css **Plugin CSS link** [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/third\_party/imageFileRobot.min.css](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/third_party/imageFileRobot.min.css)

## Example:

```
new FroalaEditor('.selector', {
  pluginsEnabled: ['image', 'imageFilerobot']
});

```

pages.title: Files Manager
pages.markdown:
# Files Manager

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Events](#events "Events")
-   [Examples](#examples "Examples")

File manager plugin allows users to upload any type of file not just images through an uploading button, drag-and-drop, URL, or embedding code. You can use it to upload single or multiple files simultaneously. It enables users also to insert, view, and delete the uploaded files.

  

## Plugin options:

[**filesManagerAllowedTypes**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#filesManagerAllowedTypes)  
Array - Default: \['\*'\]

The list of file types that are allowed to be uploaded. Although this will restrict uploading other types of files, we strongly recommend you to check the file type on the server too.

[**filesManagerMaxSize**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#%20filesManagerMaxSize)  
Number - Default: 1024 \* 1024 \* 10

The maximum file size allowed on upload in bytes. The default value is 10MB. Although this makes an additional check before uploading the file, it is highly recommended to check file size on your server too.

[**filesManagerUploadParams**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#filesManagerUploadParams)  
Object - Default: {}

Pass additional parameters to the file upload request.

[**filesManagerUploadToS3**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#filesManagerUploadToS3)  
Object - Default: false

Set the options for file upload to S3. All the fields from the example below are required. Also make sure that you have enabled CORS on Amazon.

[**filesManagerUploadURL**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#filesManagerUploadURL)  
String - Default:'http://i.froala.com/upload'

The URL where the files uploaded by the user are saved. When a file is uploaded, the editor sends the file to the server through a HTTP request. The server should process the data from the file parameter of the request and return a JSON object containing a link field with the link to the uploaded file.

  

## Plugin events:

[**filesManager.beforeUpload (files)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filesManager.beforeUpload)  

Triggered before uploading a file to the server.  

* * *

**● files:** An array with the files to be uploaded.

[**filesManager.error (error, response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filesManager.error)  

Triggered before uploading a file to the server.  
**Note:** Returning false in the handler assigned to the event will cancel the current action.

* * *

**● error** An object containing error code and description.  
**● response** Response object received from server.

[**filesManager.uploaded (response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filesManager.uploaded)  

Triggered after the file was uploaded.  
**Note:** Returning false in the handler assigned to the event will cancel the current action.

* * *

**● response** The original server response.

[**filesManager.uploadedToS3 (link, key, response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filesManager.uploadedToS3)  

Triggered after the file was uploaded to S3.  
**Note:** Returning false in the handler assigned to the event will cancel the current action.

* * *

**● link** The link to the uploaded file.  
**● key** The key of the uploaded file.  
**● response** The original server response.  

  

## Add Plugin to your code:

**Plugin name:** filesManager

**Plugin JS Script:** ../js/plugins/files\_manager.min.js

Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/files\_manager.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/files_manager.min.js)

## Example:

[Files Manager](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/examples/file-manager/)

-   [Image Management in Express Framework: Froala Node.JS SDK](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/image-management-in-express-framework-froala-node-js-sdk/)

pages.markdown:
# Filestack Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Events](#events "Events")
-   [Examples](#examples "Examples")

Empower users to utilize Filestack's robust features in their editing experience, ensuring a faster, more reliable file upload process along with advanced image and file transformation capabilities.

  

## Plugin options:

[**filestackOptions.filestackAPI**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#filestackOptions.filestackAPI)  
String - Default: ""

Your Filestack API key. To get your Filestack API, [create a free Filestack account](https://www.filestack.com/signup-free-froala/).

[**filestackOptions.uploadToFilestackOnly**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#filestackOptions.uploadToFilestackOnly)  
Boolean - Default: false

Toggle between Basic and Filestack-only modes. When enabled, images, videos, and files can be uploaded exclusively through Filestack.

[**filestackOptions.pickerOptions**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#filestackOptions.pickerOptions)  
Object - Default: {}

Configuration options for the Filestack File Picker. [See available options](https://www.filestack.com/docs/uploads/pickers/web/) in the Filestack documentation.

  

## Plugin events:

[**filestack.uploadedToFilestack (response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filestack.uploadedToFilestack)  

Triggered after successful file upload to the Filestack server.

[**filestack.uploadFailedToFilestack (response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#filestack.uploadFailedToFilestack)

Triggered after the file upload to the Filestack server fails.

Triggered when Filestack Picker is opened.

pages.title: Find and Replace Plugin
pages.markdown:
# Find and Replace Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Methods](#methods "Methods")
-   [Events](#events "Events")

The Find and Replace plugin allows users to quickly locate specific text within a document and replace it with new content. This feature enhances the editing process by streamlining text modifications, increasing efficiency, and ensuring consistency throughout the document. It is especially useful for making bulk content changes without manually searching through the text.

  

## Plugin options:

[**enableMatchCase**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#enableMatchCase)  
Boolean

If set to true, case-sensitive search will be enabled by default when the plugin is initialized.  

* * *

Default: false

[**enableMatchWholeWord**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#enableMatchWholeWord)  
Boolean

If set to true, the \`match whole word\` search will be enabled by default when the plugin is initialized.

* * *

Default: false

[**showFindAndReplace**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#showFindAndReplace)  
Boolean

If set to true, the Find and Replace popup will be displayed automatically when the editor is initialized.

* * *

Default: false

  

## Plugin methods:

[**findReplace.findMatches (searchText)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.findMatches)  

* * *

  
  
returns: -

Finds all matches of searchText in the editor content and highlights them.

* * *

**● searchText:**  
The text you are looking for.

* * *

Type: String

[**findReplace.findNextMatch (index)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.findNextMatch)  

* * *

  
  
returns: -

Navigates to the match with the given index and highlights it as the current match in focus.

* * *

**● index:**  
The index of the search text.

* * *

Type: Integer

[**findReplace.findPreviousMatch (index)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.findPreviousMatch)  

* * *

  
  
  
returns: -

Navigates to the match at the specified index in a circular backward manner and highlights it as the current match in focus.

* * *

**● index:**  
The index of the search text.

* * *

Type: Integer

[**findReplace.replaceMatch (replaceText)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.replaceMatch)  

* * *

  
  
returns: -

Replaces all matches with the given replaceText

* * *

**● replaceText:**  
The text to replace the search text.

* * *

Type: String

[**findReplace.replaceMatches (replaceText)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.findReplace.replaceMatches)  

* * *

  
  
returns: -

Finds all matches of searchText in the editor content and highlights them.

* * *

  
**● searchText:**  
The text you are looking for.

* * *

Type: String

[**findReplace.getMatchesCount ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.getMatchesCount)  

* * *

returns: Integer

Returns the total number of matches found

[**findReplace.getCurrentMatch()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.getCurrentMatch)  

* * *

returns: string/null

Returns the text content of the current match.

[**findReplace.getCurrentMatchIndex ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.getCurrentMatchIndex)  

* * *

returns: Integer

Returns the index of the current match in focus or -1 if no match is selected.

[**findReplace.showPopup ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.showPopup)  

* * *

returns: -

Show Find and Replace popup.

[**findReplace.hidePopup ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#findReplace.hidePopup)  

* * *

returns: -

Hide Find and Replace popup.

  

## Plugin events:

[**findandreplace.beforeClose ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#findandreplace.beforeClose)  

Triggered before closing the Find and Replace popup.

[**findandreplace.beforeOnReplace ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#findandreplace.beforeOnReplace)  

Triggered before replacing the matching content.

[**findandreplace.onReplace (\[{ oldValue: oldText, newValue: replaceText }\])**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#findandreplace.onReplace)  

Triggered on successful replace of match.

[**findandreplace.onReplaceAll ((\[{ oldValue: oldText, newValue: replaceText }\])**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#findandreplace.onReplaceAll)  

Triggered on successful replacement of all the matches.

  

## Add Plugin to your code:

**Plugin name:** findReplace

**Plugin JS Script:** ../js/plugins/find\_and\_replace.min.js

Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/find\_and\_replace.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/find_and_replace.min.js)

**Plugin CSS link:** ../css/plugins/find\_and\_replace.min.css

Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/plugins/find\_and\_replace.min.css](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/css/plugins/find_and_replace.min.css)

## Additional Resources

-   [Creating and Editing Web Content with a Distraction-Free Rich Text HTML Editor Software](https://froala.com/blog/editor/creating-and-editing-web-content-with-a-distraction-free-rich-text-html-editor-software/)
-   [Unlock the Power of Customizable Toolbars with Froala](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/unlock-the-power-of-customizable-toolbars-with-froala/)

pages.title: Font Awesome Plugin
pages.markdown:
# Font Awesome Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Examples](#examples "Examples")

Adds the web's most popular icon set and toolkit to your editor.

Allow your users to Insert Font Awesome icons in the editor text.

  

## Plugin options:

[**faButtons**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#faButtons)  
Array -

The list of Font Awesome buttons to show in the popup for inserting icons.

* * *

Default: \["fontAwesomeBack", "|"\]

[**fontAwesomeSets**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fontAwesomeSets)  
Object -

The list of Font Awesome icons to show in the modal for inserting icons.

* * *

Default: {}

[**fontAwesomeTemplate**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fontAwesomeTemplate)  
String -

Set the template to be used for the Font Awesome icons inserted in the editor.

pages.title: Import from Word Plugin
pages.markdown:
# Import from Word Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Methods](#methods "Methods")
-   [Events](#events "Events")
-   [Dependencies](#dependencies "Dependencies")

Import .docx files directly into the editor with formatting intact. Headings, lists, and images transfer automatically, with support for both client-side (Mammoth.js) and server-side conversion.

  

## Plugin options:

[**importFromWordMaxFileSize**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#importFromWordMaxFileSize)  
Number

The maximum allowed file size in bytes.

* * *

Default: 3 \* 1024 \* 1024

[**importFromWordFileTypesAllowed**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#importFromWordFileTypesAllowed)  
Array

A list of allowed file extensions.

* * *

Default: \['docx'\]

[**importFromWordUrlToUpload**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#importFromWordUrlToUpload)  
String

The URL of a server-side handler for conversion. If null, client-side conversion via mammoth.js is used.

* * *

Default: null

[**importFromWordEnableImportOnDrop**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#importFromWordEnableImportOnDrop)  
Boolean

Whether to trigger the import process when a valid Word file is dropped into the editor.

* * *

Default: true

[**importFromWordMammoth**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#importFromWordMammoth)  
Object

Specifies the Mammoth library instance used to import and convert Microsoft Word (.docx) documents into HTML content.

* * *

Default: window.mammoth

  

## Plugin methods:

[**importFromWord.import (file)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#importFromWord.import)

Opens the file selection dialog or processes a provided File object.

* * *

**● File (object):** optional , The `File` object to be converted and imported.

  

## Plugin events:

[**word.beforeImport (file)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#word.beforeImport)

Triggered before the file processing starts. Returning false will cancel the import.

[**word.afterImport (html)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#word.afterImport)

Triggered after the content has been converted and inserted into the editor.

  

## Dependencies

The Import from Word plugin allows users to import .docx files directly into the Froala Editor. It supports both client-side conversion (via Mammoth.js) and server-side conversion.

For client-side conversion (when importFromWordUrlToUpload is null), the plugin requires Mammoth.js to be loaded on the page:

```
  <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/mammoth/1.4.21/mammoth.browser.min.js"></script>
```

  

## Add Plugin to your code:

**Plugin name:** importFromWord

**Plugin JS Script:** ../js/plugins/import\_from\_word.min.js

Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/import\_from\_word.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/import_from_word.min.js)

## Additional Resources

    -   [From Word to Froala in Seconds: Mastering Import from Word Plugin](https://froala.com/blog/editor/import-word-documents-froala-editor/)

# Lists Plugin

Allows users to insert lists in the editor, not just the basic lists like numbers and bullets but also advanced types such as lower greek or upper roman.

[**listAdvancedTypes**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#listAdvancedTypes)  
Boolean

Enables list advanced types for the bullets.

* * *

  
Default: true

  

[**preserveListMarkerStyle**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#preserveListMarkerStyle)  
Boolean

Controls how bold and italic are saved when they are applied to a whole list item. When set to true, the formatting is added to the `<li>` element as `font-weight` or `font-style`, so the bullet or number is also bold or italic. When set to false, the editor keeps semantic `<strong>` and `<em>` tags inside the item and leaves the marker unchanged. Set it to false when your content goes to email templates, screen-reader-sensitive pages, or a Markdown export, where semantic tags work better than inline styles. Default: true

* * *

  
Default: true

headings: The list of Froala Markdown Syntax:
pages.markdown:
# Markdown plugin

Format words & phrases in our rich text editor using code shortcuts through [predefined markdown syntax](https://froala.com/blog/general/markdown-to-html-editors-bridging-the-gap-for-developers/).

When in markdown mode, the Froala Editor provides an easy split screen view so users can see the changes in real-time.

Users can markdown Heading, Bold Text ,Italic, Blockquote, Ordered list , Unordered list, Code, Fenced code block, Horizontal rule, Link , Image, Table, Footnote , Strikethrough and Task list.

## The list of Froala Markdown Syntax:

  

Element

Markdown Syntax (Code)

Heading

\# H1  
\## H2  
\### H3

Heading ID

\### My Great Heading {#custom-id}

Bold

\*\*bold text\*\*

Italic

\*italicized text\*

Strikethrough

~~The world is flat.~~

Blockquote

\> blockquote

Ordered List

1\. First item  
2\. Second item  
3\. Third item

Unordered List

\- First item  
\- Second item  
\- Third item

emphasis

\* item

Code

\`code\`

Fenced Code Block

\`\`\`  
{  
“firstName”: “John”,  
“lastName”: “Smith”,  
“age”: 25  
}  
\`\`\`

Horizontal Rule

\---

Link

\[title\](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/markdown-plugin/%3Chttps://www.example.com%3E "title")

Image

!\[alt text\](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/markdown-plugin/image.jpg)

Table

| Syntax | Description |  
| --- | ---|  
| Header | Title |  
| Paragraph | Text |

Footnote

Here’s a sentence with a footnote. \[^1\]  
\[^1\]: This is the footnote.

Definition List

term  
: definition

Task List

\- \[x\] Write the press release  
\- \[ \] Update the website  
\- \[ \] Contact the media

  

For example, to denote a heading, users can add a hashtag before the word (e.g. #Heading1, #Heading2). Or to italicize text, \*italic text\*. Users can also markdown Bold Text, Blockquotes, Ordered or Unordered lists, Code blocks, Images, Task lists, and many more!

## Plugin methods:

[**markdown.isEnabled ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#markdown.isEnabled)  
returns: boolean

Find if markdown mode is active.

[**markdown.toggle ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#markdown.toggle)  
returns: –

Toggle between the markdown and text view.

[**markdown.refresh ($btn)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#markdown.refresh)  
returns: Array

Check if the markdown is enabled and set the state of the markdown button.

* * *

-   **$btn:** The markdown button element.

Type: DOM Object

[**markdown.getMarkdown ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#markdown.getMarkdown)  
returns: String | Boolean

Returns the current Markdown content as a string or false if `markdown.beforeGet` cancels the read.

[**markdown.setMarkdown (markdown)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#markdown.setMarkdown)  
returns: Boolean | null

Replaces the Markdown editor’s content with a given Markdown string.

* * *

**markdown:** String containing the markdown to load. Non-string values are rejected.  
Type: String

## Plugin Events:

[**markdown.beforeGet**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#markdown.beforeGet)

Fires before `getMarkdown()` reads the content; returning `false` cancels the read.

[**markdown.afterGet (markdown)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#markdown.afterGet)

Fires after `getMarkdown()` has retrieved the content.

* * *

-   **markdown:** The markdown string that was returned.

[**markdown.beforeSet (markdown)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#markdown.beforeSet)

Fires before `setMarkdown()` applies new content; returning `false` cancels the set.

* * *

-   **markdown:** The markdown string passed to `setMarkdown()`.

[**markdown.set**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#markdown.set)

Fires after `setMarkdown()` has successfully applied the content.

**Plugin JS Script:**

Or from CDN

pages.markdown:
# Save Plugin

-   [Options](#options "Options")
-   [Methods](#methods "Methods")
-   [Events](#events "Events")

Enables [AJAX saving](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/save/button/%20) of the content inside the editor, and you can set the editor to autosave the content and no worries then about data loss, Our rich text editor automatically makes a save request to your server as the user types.

  

## Plugin options:

[**saveInterval**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#saveInterval)  
Number -

Time in milliseconds that defines when the autosave should be triggered. Setting a higher interval helps prevent request overload on the server. The autosave will be triggered only if the content was changed from the last interval. Setting the value to 0 will disable autosave.  
**Note:** It is not recommended to use values lower than 2000ms in order to prevent overload.

* * *

  
Default: 10000

[**saveMethod**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#saveMethod)  
String -

The HTTP save request type.

* * *

  
Default: 'POST'

[**saveParam**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#saveParam)  
String -

The name of the parameter which contains the rich text editor's content on the save request.

* * *

  
Default: 'body'

[**saveParams**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#saveParams)  
Object -

Additional parameters passed to the save request.

* * *

  
Default: {}

[**saveURL**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#saveURL)  
String -

The URL where the save request is being made. The editor will initialize a HTTP request to the specified URL passing the editor's content in the body parameter of the HTTP request.

* * *

  
Default: null

  

## Plugin methods:

[**save.force ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#save.force)  
returns: Object

Force a save request at the end of the current autosave interval.

[**save.save ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#save.save)  
returns: Object

Initializes a save request to the URL specified by the saveURL option.

[**save.reset ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#save.resete)  
returns: Object

Restore the force request at the end of the current autosave interval.

  

## Plugin events:

[**save.after (data)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#save.after)  
.

Triggered after the save request.

* * *

**● data**  
The returned data from the save request

[**save.before (html)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#save.before)  
.

Triggered before doing the save request. If a string is returned, the new string will be used as the saved content.  
**Note:** Returning false in the handler assigned to the event will cancel the current action.

* * *

  
**● html**  
The HTML to save.

[**save.error (error, response)**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#save.error)  
.

Triggered when an error occurs during save request.

* * *

  
**● error**  
The description of the error that happened during the save request.  
**● response**  
The original response from the server.

  

## Add Plugin to your code:

**Plugin name:** save

**Plugin JS Script:** ../js/plugins/save.min.js

Or from CDN [https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/save.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/froala-editor@latest/js/plugins/save.min.js)

**Plugin CSS link:**

pages.markdown:
# Track changes plugin

This feature enables Froala Editor to keep track of all the changes users make to their text, images, tables, styles, formatting, and more followed by accepting and rejecting the changes accordingly through easy access to ‘Accept or Reject’ a ‘Single or All’ changes via accessible buttons in the toolbar. Additionally track addition and deletion of text, images, tables. Additionally styling and formatting changes to text, images, tables.

## Track changes feature includes the following functionalities:

-   Enable / disable track changes – Users can enable and disable the track changes feature on Froala editor.
-   Show / hide tracked changes – Users can show or hide the changes made on the Froala editor.
-   Accept / Reject Single change – Users can track and ACCEPT or REJECT the single / last change that are made on the editor
-   Accept / Reject ALL changes – Users can track and ACCEPT or REJECT ALL changes that are made on the editor

With Track Changes enabled, any text or image additions are shown with a yellow highlight and changes that are intended to be deleted are highlighted in red with a strikethrough.

  

## Plugin options:

  

[**trackChangesEnabled**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#trackChangesEnabled)  
Boolean- Default: false

If set to true, track changes will be active by default.

[**showChangesEnabled**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#showChangesEnabled)  
Boolean- Default: false

If set to true, show changes will be active by default.

  

## Plugin methods:

  

[**track\_changes.toggleTracking ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#track_changes.toggleTracking)  
returns: -

Enable/Disable track changes

[**track\_changes.showChanges ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#track_changes.showChanges)  
returns: -

show/hide tracked changes

[**track\_changes.getPendingChanges ()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#track_changes.getPendingChanges)  
returns: Array

Return all tracked changes.

[**track\_changes.acceptAllChanges()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#track_changes.acceptAllChanges)  
returns: -

Accept all changes that are made on the editor

[**track\_changes.acceptSingleChange()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#track_changes.acceptSingleChange)  
returns: -

Accept the last change that are made on the editor

[**track\_changes.rejectSingleChange()**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/#track_changes.rejectSingleChange)  
returns: -

Reject the last change that are made on the editor

  

## Plugin commands:

returns: Object

Show more track changes actions toolbar.

pages.markdown:
# Server SDKs

Froala has server SDKs for six languages. Each one answers the requests the editor sends to your server, to store, delete and list images and files and to sign uploads to Amazon S3.

## About

Pick your language. Its guide covers installing the SDK and each task below.

| SDK | Install | Repository | Code last changed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [.NET](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/dotnet/) | `dotnet add package FroalaEditorSDK`, from NuGet | [wysiwyg-editor-dotnet-sdk](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-dotnet-sdk) | February 2019 |
| [Java](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/java/) | No package. Add `Lib/wysiwyg-editor-java-sdk.jar` from the repository. | [wysiwyg-editor-java-sdk](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-java-sdk) | February 2019 |
| [Node.js](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/nodejs/) | `npm install wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk` | [wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-node-sdk) | July 2026 |
| [PHP](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/php/) | `composer require froala/wysiwyg-editor-php-sdk` | [wysiwyg-editor-php-sdk](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-php-sdk) | July 2023 |
| [Python](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/python/) | No package. Copy the `froala_editor` folder from the repository. | [wysiwyg-editor-python-sdk](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-python-sdk) | April 2019 |
| [Ruby](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/ruby/) | `gem 'froala-editor-sdk'` in your Gemfile | [wysiwyg-editor-ruby-sdk](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-ruby-sdk) | February 2019 |

The Node.js SDK also runs the server side of real-time collaboration. See [Collaboration Overview](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/nodejs/collaboration-overview/).

Every SDK gets a new version with each editor release, and most of those releases change only the version number. The last column gives the date of the last change to the SDK's own code.

### Before You Pick One

- The .NET SDK builds for `net471` and `netstandard2.0`, the second against the ASP.NET Core packages at `2.2.0`.
- .NET Core `2.2`, the release those packages belong to, has been out of support since December 2019.
- The .NET package's .NET Standard build asks for `Magick.NET.Core-Q16 >= 7.10.2`, a version NuGet doesn't have, so it may not restore in an ASP.NET Core project. Referencing the repository's `src` project avoids that.
- The Java jar was built in March 2017, before video upload was added to the source. Build the `Lib` project for video upload.
- The Java SDK uses `javax.servlet`. Tomcat 10 and later moved to `jakarta.servlet`, so it runs on Tomcat 9 and other `javax` containers, or after migration.
- Packagist lists the PHP SDK up to `5.2.0`. Its later releases are tags in the repository.

## Image

Each SDK's guides cover these tasks for images, and what the editor needs for each.

| Task | In the editor |
| --- | --- |
| Server Upload | `imageUploadURL` points at the action that stores the image. |
| Server Delete | The `image.removed` and `image.replaced` events, where your code asks the server to delete the file. |
| S3 Upload | `imageUploadToS3` takes the signature your server computes. |
| Resize | Nothing more. The server resizes the image as it stores it. |
| Validation | `imageAllowedTypes` and `imageMaxSize` check in the browser, and the server checks again. |

## Image Manager

The image manager sends your server two requests.

| Request | Option | The server answers with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Load the images | `imageManagerLoadURL` | A list of images, each with its `url` and `thumb`. |
| Delete an image | `imageManagerDeleteURL` | A success status, once it has deleted the image named in `src`. |

## File

The guides cover the same tasks for files, except resizing.

| Task | In the editor |
| --- | --- |
| Server Upload | `fileUploadURL` points at the action that stores the file. |
| Server Delete | The `file.unlink` event, where your code asks the server to delete the file. |
| S3 Upload | `fileUploadToS3` takes the signature your server computes. |
| Validation | `fileAllowedTypes` and `fileMaxSize` check in the browser, and the server checks again. |

## Additional Resources

- [6 Server Side Frameworks With WYSIWYG Editor Integration](https://froala.com/blog/general/6-server-side-frameworks-with-wysiwyg-editor-integration/)

# .NET SDK

The .NET SDK does the editor's server side work in ASP.NET. It stores uploaded images, files and videos, deletes them, lists images for the image manager and signs uploads that go straight to Amazon S3. Its source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-dotnet-sdk), under the MIT license.

## About

One library serves ASP.NET Core and ASP.NET MVC on .NET Framework. It builds for `net471` and `netstandard2.0`, and its classes live in the `FroalaEditor` namespace. The repository has a working app for each, [demo-core](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-dotnet-sdk/tree/master/demo-core/) for ASP.NET Core and [demo](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-dotnet-sdk/tree/master/demo/) for ASP.NET MVC.

The SDK's code last changed in February 2019. Its releases since then, the latest in September 2026, only raise the version number to match the editor's. The .NET Standard build references the ASP.NET Core packages at `2.2.0`, a release out of support since December 2019, and demo-core targets `netcoreapp2.0`. Test it in your app before you rely on it.

## Download

Clone the repository or [download it as a ZIP](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-dotnet-sdk/archive/master.zip), then reference its `src` project from yours. In Visual Studio, right-click your project and choose Add, Reference, Projects, then `src`. From the command line, run these two commands.

```shell
git clone https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-dotnet-sdk.git
dotnet add reference wysiwyg-editor-dotnet-sdk/src/src.csproj
```

## Or Use NuGet

The package is [FroalaEditorSDK](https://www.nuget.org/packages/FroalaEditorSDK). Install it from the Package Manager Console in Visual Studio.

```shell
Install-Package FroalaEditorSDK
```

Or with the .NET CLI.

```shell
dotnet add package FroalaEditorSDK
```

The package's .NET Standard build depends on `Magick.NET.Core-Q16 >= 7.10.2`, and NuGet has no such version. That package is deprecated and stops at `7.0.5.900`, so expect the restore to fail in an ASP.NET Core project. Reference the `src` project instead, as in [Download](#download). The .NET Framework build depends on `Magick.NET-Q16-AnyCPU`, which NuGet has.

## Classes

Each class is static. Call it from the controller action the editor sends its request to.

| Class | Methods | Options | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FroalaEditor.Image` | `Upload`, `Delete`, `List` | `ImageOptions`, `ImageValidation` | [Image Reference](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/dotnet/references/image/) |
| `FroalaEditor.File` | `Upload`, `Delete` | `FileOptions`, `FileValidation` | [File Reference](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/dotnet/references/file/) |
| `FroalaEditor.Video` | `Upload`, `Delete` | `VideoOptions`, `VideoValidation` | Works like `File`. It accepts mp4, webm and ogg by default. |
| `FroalaEditor.S3` | `GetHash` | `S3Config` | [S3 Reference](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/dotnet/references/s3/) |

- [Image Server Delete](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/dotnet/image-server-delete/)
- [Image S3 Upload](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/dotnet/image-s3-upload/)

# .NET SDK File Reference

## Upload (httpContext, fileRoute, options)

Returns `object`.

Method used to upload a file to a specified location on disk.

### **Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `httpContext` | HttpContext | All the HTTP specific information for the HTTP request. |
| `fileRoute` | String | The server route for file uploads. This route must be public. |
| `options` | FileOptions | This parameter is optional. It is used to pass custom options for the file upload. |

Short example of `options`.

```csharp
FroalaEditor.FileOptions options = new FroalaEditor.FileOptions
{
    Fieldname = "myFile",
    Validation = new FroalaEditor.FileValidation(yourCustomValidationFunction)
};
```

### **options parameter**

- **Fieldname** Tag name that points to the file.  Type.StringDefault."file"
- **Validation** Specify the allowed file extensions and mimetypes.  Type.FileValidationDefault./// Allowed file validation default extensions. public static string[] AllowedFileExtsDefault = new string[] { "txt", "pdf", "doc" }; /// Allowed file validation default mimetypes. public static string[] AllowedFileMimetypesDefault = new string[] { "text/plain", "application/msword", "application/x-pdf", "application/pdf" };

### **Response**

If the upload is successful, the method returns an object with one property, `link`, the folder plus the file's new name. If an error occurs, the method throws an exception.

```csharp
try
{
    return Json(FroalaEditor.File.Upload(System.Web.HttpContext.Current, uploadPath));
}
catch (Exception e)
{
    return Json(new { error = e.Message });
}
```

## Delete (filePath)

Method used to delete a file from disk. Throws an exception if an error occurs.

### **Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filePath` | String | The file's link, as `Upload` returned it. The SDK maps it to the file on disk the same way `Upload` did. |

# .NET SDK S3 Reference

## GetHash (config)

Returns `object`, a `Dictionary<string, object>`.

Method used to compute the hash that the editor uses to sign to Amazon S3 when uploading a file.

### **Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config` | S3Config | Configuration object for the Amazon S3 signature. |

### **config parameter**

- **Bucket** The name of your bucket.  Type.String
- **Region** S3 region. If you are using the default `us-east-1`, this can be ignored.  Type.String
- **KeyStart** The folder where to upload the images. End it with a slash, such as `uploads/`, because the editor adds the file name right after it.  Type.String
- **Acl** File access permission. E.g. `'public-read'`  Type.String
- **AccessKey** Your Amazon access key.  Type.String
- **SecretKey** Your Amazon secret key.  Type.String
- **Expiration** Minutes the signature stays valid, such as `"30"`. If you leave it out, the signature lasts 5 minutes.  Type.String

### **Response**

The hash the editor needs in `imageUploadToS3` or `fileUploadToS3` if you want to upload an image or a file to Amazon S3.

The Java SDK for Froala Editor is designed to work with HttpServlet. To help you integrate the Javascript editor even faster, you can use the examples from the SDK ([Java Examples](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-java-sdk/tree/master/Examples)).

# Java SDK S3 Reference

## getHash (config)

Returns a `Map<Object, Object>`.

Method used to compute the [hash used by the javascript editor](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/sdks/java/file-s3-upload/) to sign to Amazon S3 when uploading a file.

### **Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config` | `S3Config` | Configuration object for the Amazon S3 signature. |

### **config parameter**

- **bucket** The name of your bucket.  Type.String
- **region** S3 region. If you are using the default `us-east-1`, this can be ignored.  Type.String
- **keyStart** The folder where to upload the images. End it with a slash, such as `uploads/`, because the editor adds the file name right after it.  Type.String
- **acl** File access permission. E.g. `'public-read'`  Type.String
- **accessKey** Your Amazon access key.  Type.String
- **secretKey** Your Amazon secret key.  Type.String

### **Response**

The hash that needs to be passed to the javascript editor, in `imageUploadToS3` or `fileUploadToS3`, if you want to upload an image or a file to Amazon S3. It is a map with the `bucket`, the `region`, the `keyStart` and the signed `params`.

# PHP SDK

[GitHub](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-php-sdk)

## Download

Get Froala rich text editor running with our PHP SDK library by hitting the download link below.

[Download PHP SDK](https://github.com/froala/wysiwyg-editor-php-sdk/archive/master.zip)

## Or Use Composer

Composer is a package manager for PHP. In the composer.json file in your project add the Froala WYSIWYG Editor PHP SDK.

```json
{
  "require" : {
    "froala/wysiwyg-editor-php-sdk" : "^5.2"
  }
}
```

And then run.

```shell
php composer.phar install
```

## Import the SDK in your app

```php
require 'PATH_TO_FROALA_SDK/lib/FroalaEditor.php';
```

Please make sure your server has the [FileInfo](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.fileinfo.php) and [Imagick](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.imagick.php) extensions enabled. The SDK needs both, for files as well as images.

## upload ($fileRoute, $options)

Method used to upload file to the specified location on disk.

### **Parameters**

| --- | --- | --- |
| `$fileRoute` | String | The path relative to the `$_SERVER['DOCUMENT_ROOT']` global variable were the file should be uploaded. |

try {

  echo stripslashes(json_encode($response));
} catch (Exception $e) {
  http_response_code(404);
}
```

If the upload is completed successfully, the method returns an object with the absolute path to the uploaded image. If an error occurs, the method throws an exception.

```php
